sentences.zh: 【晉紀二十六】起柔兆困敦，盡玄黓敦牂，凡七年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 26] From Rouzhao Kundun through Xuanyi Dunzang; seven years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals 26] From Rouzhao Kundun through Xuanyi Dunzang—seven years in all.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝上之中太元元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — first year of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — first year of Taiyuan (

sentences.zh: 丙子，公元三七六年）

translations.literal: bingzi, corresponding to 376 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingzi year, 376 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬寅朔，帝加元服，皇太后下詔歸政，復稱崇德太后。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the first day of the month (ren-yin), the Emperor performed the coming-of-age ceremony; the Empress Dowager issued an edict restoring the throne to him and resumed the title Empress Dowager Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on New Year's Day, the Emperor came of age. The Empress Dowager issued an edict returning the government to him and resumed the title Empress Dowager Chongde.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On jiachen, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 丙午，帝始臨朝。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the Emperor began to hold court in person.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the Emperor began to preside over court in person.

sentences.zh: 以會稽內史郗愔為鎮軍大將軍、都督浙江東五郡諸軍事；

translations.literal: Xi Yin, Interior Minister of Kuaiji, was made General Who Stabilizes the Army and given command over all military affairs in the five commanderies east of the Zhe River;
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yin, Interior Minister of Kuaiji, was appointed General Who Stabilizes the Army and placed in command of all military affairs in the five commanderies east of the Zhe River;

sentences.zh: 徐州刺史桓沖為車騎將軍、都督豫、江二州之六郡諸軍事，自京口徙鎮姑孰。

translations.literal: Huan Chong, Inspector of Xuzhou, was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and given command over military affairs in six commanderies of Yu and Jiang provinces, moving his headquarters from Jingkou to Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong, Inspector of Xuzhou, was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and given command over six commanderies in Yu and Jiang provinces, transferring his headquarters from Jingkou to Gushu.

sentences.zh: 謝安欲以王蘊為方伯，故先解沖徐州。

translations.literal: Xie An wished to appoint Wang Yun as a regional governor, so he first removed Huan Chong from Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An wanted to appoint Wang Yun as a regional governor, so he first relieved Huan Chong of his post in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，加謝安中書監，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On yimao, Xie An was additionally appointed Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Xie An was additionally made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and put in charge of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯，秦王堅下詔曰：「朕聞王者勞於求賢，逸於得士，斯言何其驗也！

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinmao, King Fu Jian of Qin issued an edict saying: "I have heard that kings toil in seeking the worthy and rest once they have obtained men of talent. How true these words prove!
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinmao, King Fu Jian of Qin issued an edict: "I have heard that a ruler toils to find worthy men and only rests once he has won their service. How true that saying proves!

sentences.zh: 往得丞相，常謂帝王易為。

translations.literal: When I obtained a Chancellor, I often said that being a ruler was easy.
translations.idiomatic: Once I had a Chancellor at my side, I often said that ruling was easy.

sentences.zh: 自丞相違世，鬚髮中白，每一念之，不覺酸慟。

translations.literal: Since the Chancellor departed this world, my hair and beard have turned half white; each time I think of him, I cannot help but feel grief.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Chancellor left this world, my hair and beard have gone half white, and each time I think of him I am overcome with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 今天下既無丞相，或政教淪替，可分遣侍臣周巡郡縣，問民疾苦。」

translations.literal: Now that there is no Chancellor under Heaven, government and moral instruction may have fallen into disorder; palace attendants may be dispatched to tour the commanderies and counties and inquire after the people's hardships."
translations.idiomatic: Now that there is no Chancellor in the realm, government and moral instruction may have fallen into decay. Let palace attendants be sent to tour the commanderies and counties and inquire into the people's hardships."

sentences.zh: 三月，秦兵寇南鄉，拔之，山蠻三萬戶降秦。

translations.literal: In the third month, Qin troops raided Nanxiang, took it, and thirty thousand households of mountain barbarians submitted to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Qin forces attacked Nanxiang, captured it, and thirty thousand households of mountain tribes submitted to Qin.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，甲寅，大赦。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on jiayin, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on jiayin, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 初，張天錫之殺張邕也，劉肅及安定梁景皆有功，二人由是有寵，賜姓張氏，以為己子，使預政事。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang Tiansun killed Zhang Yong, Liu Su and Liang Jing of Anding had both rendered meritorious service; the two men thereby gained favor, were granted the surname Zhang, and were treated as his own sons and allowed to participate in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Tiansun killed Zhang Yong, Liu Su and Liang Jing of Anding had both distinguished themselves in the affair. The two men thereby won his favor: he granted them the surname Zhang, treated them as his own sons, and let them take part in government.

sentences.zh: 天錫荒於酒色，不親庶務，黜世子大懷而立嬖妾焦氏之子大豫，以焦氏為左夫人，人情憤怨。

translations.literal: Tiansun was dissolute in wine and women and did not attend to routine affairs; he deposed the heir apparent Dahua and established Dayu, son of his favorite concubine Lady Jiao, making Lady Jiao Left Lady, and popular sentiment was angry and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansun abandoned himself to wine and women and neglected the daily business of rule. He deposed the heir apparent Dahua and installed Dayu, the son of his favorite concubine Lady Jiao, making Lady Jiao his Left Lady. Public sentiment turned angry and resentful.

sentences.zh: 從弟從事中郎憲輿櫬切諫，不聽。

translations.literal: His younger cousin, Attendant Gentleman Xian, carried a coffin and remonstrated urgently, but Tiansun would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin, Attendant Gentleman Xian, brought a coffin and remonstrated with desperate urgency, but Tiansun refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅下詔曰：「張天錫雖稱籓受位，然臣道未純，可遣使持節、武衛將軍武都苟萇、左將軍毛盛、中書令梁熙、步兵校尉姚萇等將兵臨西河，尚書郎閻負、梁殊奉詔徵天錫入朝，若有違王命，即進師撲討。」

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin issued an edict saying: "Although Zhang Tiansun has declared himself a vassal and accepted investiture, his conduct as a subject is not pure. An envoy bearing credentials may be sent: Military Guard General Gou Chang of Wudu, Left General Mao Sheng, Palace Secretary Liang Xi, and Footsoldier Commandant Yao Chang and others shall lead troops to the western river; Masters of Writing Yan Fu and Liang Shu shall carry the edict summoning Tiansun to court. If he disobeys the royal command, advance the army at once to suppress and chastise him."
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin issued an edict: "Although Zhang Tiansun has declared himself a vassal and accepted office, his loyalty as a subject is not complete. Let an envoy bearing credentials be sent: Military Guard General Gou Chang of Wudu, Left General Mao Sheng, Palace Secretary Liang Xi, and Footsoldier Commandant Yao Chang shall lead troops to the western frontier; Masters of Writing Yan Fu and Liang Shu shall carry the edict summoning Tiansun to court. If he defies the royal command, advance at once and crush him."

sentences.zh: 是時，秦步騎十三萬，軍司段鏗謂周颺曰：「以此眾戰，誰能敵之！」

translations.literal: At this time Qin had one hundred thirty thousand infantry and cavalry. Army Director Duan Kan said to Zhou Xiao: "With this force to fight, who could stand against it!"
translations.idiomatic: At this time Qin fielded one hundred thirty thousand infantry and cavalry. Army Director Duan Kan said to Zhou Xiao, "With an army like this, who could stand against us?"

sentences.zh: 虓曰：「戎狄以來，未之有也。」

translations.literal: Xiao said: "Since the barbarian tribes, there has never been such a thing."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao replied, "Since the age of the barbarian tribes, nothing like it has ever been seen."

sentences.zh: 堅又命秦州刺史苟池、河州刺史李辯、涼州刺史王統帥三州之眾為苟萇後繼。

translations.literal: Fu Jian further ordered Gou Chi, Inspector of Qinzhou; Li Bian, Inspector of Hezhou; and Wang Tong, Inspector of Liangzhou, to lead the forces of the three provinces as Gou Chang's rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian also ordered Gou Chi, Inspector of Qinzhou; Li Bian, Inspector of Hezhou; and Wang Tong, Inspector of Liangzhou, to bring the armies of their three provinces as Gou Chang's reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，閻負、梁殊至姑臧。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Yan Fu and Liang Shu arrived at Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Yan Fu and Liang Shu reached Guzang.

sentences.zh: 張天錫會官屬謀之，曰：「今入朝，必不返；

translations.literal: Zhang Tiansun convened his officials to deliberate, saying: "If I go to court now, I will surely not return;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tiansun gathered his officials to discuss the matter. He said, "If I go to court now, I will never return;

sentences.zh: 如其不從，秦兵必至，將若之何？」

translations.literal: if I do not obey, Qin troops will surely come — what then shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: and if I refuse, Qin troops will surely come. What are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 禁中錄事席仂曰：「以愛子為質，賂以重寶，以退其師，然後徐為之計，此屈伸之術也。」

translations.literal: Palace Recorder Xi Le said: "Offer a beloved son as hostage, bribe them with precious treasures to withdraw their army, and then slowly devise a plan — this is the art of yielding and advancing."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Recorder Xi Le said, "Send a beloved son as hostage, offer rich treasures to buy off their army, and then plan your next move at leisure. That is the way to bend without breaking."

sentences.zh: 眾皆怒曰：「吾世事晉朝，忠節著於海內。

translations.literal: All were angry and said: "Our family has served the Jin dynasty for generations; loyalty and integrity are renowned throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly erupted in anger. "Our house has served the Jin dynasty for generations," they said. "Our loyalty is known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 今一旦委身賊庭，辱及祖宗，丑莫大焉！

translations.literal: Now to cast ourselves at once into the enemy court — disgrace reaching to our ancestors — there is no greater shame!
translations.idiomatic: To throw ourselves into the enemy's camp would disgrace our ancestors — there could be no greater shame!

sentences.zh: 且河西天險，百年無虞，若悉境內精兵，右招西域，北引匈奴，以拒之，何遽知其不捷也！」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Hexi region has Heaven's natural defenses and has been secure for a century; if we mobilize all elite troops within the borders, summon the Western Regions to the right and draw in the Xiongnu from the north to resist them, how can you know so quickly that we will not prevail!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Hexi region is protected by natural barriers and has been secure for a century. If we mobilize every elite soldier in the land, summon allies from the Western Regions and draw the Xiongnu down from the north, who is to say we cannot prevail?"

sentences.zh: 天錫攘袂大言曰：「孤計決矣，言降者斬！」

translations.literal: Tiansun rolled up his sleeves and declared loudly: "My decision is made — whoever speaks of surrender shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Tiansun rolled up his sleeves and declared, "My mind is made up. Whoever speaks of surrender will be executed!"

sentences.zh: 使謂閻負、梁殊曰：「君欲生歸乎，死歸乎？」

translations.literal: He sent word to Yan Fu and Liang Shu, saying: "Do you wish to return alive, or return dead?"
translations.idiomatic: He sent word to Yan Fu and Liang Shu: "Do you wish to go home alive, or go home dead?"

sentences.zh: 殊等辭氣不屈，天錫怒，縛之軍門，命軍士交射之，曰：「射而不中，不與我同心者也。」

translations.literal: Shu and the others would not yield in word or spirit. Tiansun was enraged, bound them at the army gate, and ordered the soldiers to shoot at them in turn, saying: "Whoever shoots and misses does not share my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Shu and the others would not yield in word or bearing. Tiansun flew into a rage, had them bound at the army gate, and ordered the soldiers to shoot at them in turn. "Whoever misses," he said, "does not stand with me."

sentences.zh: 其母嚴氏泣曰：「秦主以一州之地，橫制天下，東平鮮卑，南取巴、蜀，兵不留行，所向無敵。

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Yan, wept and said: "The ruler of Qin, with the territory of a single province, holds sway over the realm: he pacified the Xianbei in the east and seized Ba and Shu in the south; his armies never linger, and wherever they go none can stand against them.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Yan, wept and said, "The ruler of Qin, starting from a single province, has brought the realm under his sway: he subdued the Xianbei in the east and seized Ba and Shu in the south. His armies never pause, and nothing has stood in their way.

sentences.zh: 汝若降之，猶可延數年之命。

translations.literal: If you submit to him, you may still prolong your life by several years.
translations.idiomatic: If you submit to him, you may yet keep your life for a few more years.

sentences.zh: 今以蕞爾一隅，抗衡大國，又殺其使者，亡無日矣！」

translations.literal: Now with this tiny corner to contend against a great state, and having killed their envoys besides — destruction will come any day!"
translations.idiomatic: But now, with this tiny corner of land, you mean to stand against a great power — and you have killed their envoys besides. Your doom will come any day!"

sentences.zh: 天錫使龍驤將軍馬建帥眾二萬拒秦。

translations.literal: Tiansun sent Dragon Cavalry General Ma Jian to command twenty thousand men to resist Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansun sent Dragon Cavalry General Ma Jian at the head of twenty thousand men to resist Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦人聞天錫殺閻負、梁殊，八月，梁熙、姚萇、王統、李辯濟自清石津，攻涼驍烈將軍梁濟於河會城，降之。

translations.literal: When the Qin people heard that Tiansun had killed Yan Fu and Liang Shu, in the eighth month Liang Xi, Yao Chang, Wang Tong, and Li Bian crossed from Qingshi Ford, attacked Liang Ji, Fierce General of Liang, at Hehui City, and accepted his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin learned that Tiansun had killed Yan Fu and Liang Shu, Liang Xi, Yao Chang, Wang Tong, and Li Bian crossed at Qingshi Ford in the eighth month, attacked Liang Ji, Fierce General of Liang, at Hehui City, and accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 甲申，苟萇濟自石城津，與梁熙等會攻纏縮城，拔之。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Gou Chang crossed from Shicheng Ford, joined Liang Xi and the others in attacking Chansuo City, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Gou Chang crossed at Shicheng Ford, joined Liang Xi and the others in the assault on Chansuo City, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 馬建懼，自楊非退屯清塞。

translations.literal: Ma Jian was afraid, withdrew from Yangfei, and encamped at Qingsai.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jian, alarmed, withdrew from Yangfei and encamped at Qingsai.

sentences.zh: 天錫又遣征東將軍掌據帥眾三萬軍於洪池，天錫自將餘眾五萬，軍於金昌城。

translations.literal: Tiansun further sent Eastern Campaign General Zhang Ju to command thirty thousand men and encamp at Hongchi; Tiansun himself led the remaining fifty thousand and encamped at Jinchang City.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansun sent Eastern Campaign General Zhang Ju with thirty thousand men to encamp at Hongchi, while he himself led the remaining fifty thousand to Jinchang City.

sentences.zh: 安西將軍敦煌宋皓言於天錫曰：「臣晝察人事，夜觀天文，秦兵不可敵也，不如降之。」

translations.literal: Song Hao of Dunhuang, General Who Pacifies the West, said to Tiansun: "Your subject observes human affairs by day and watches the heavens by night — Qin troops cannot be resisted; it would be better to submit."
translations.idiomatic: Song Hao of Dunhuang, General Who Pacifies the West, told Tiansun, "I have watched affairs by day and read the heavens by night. Qin cannot be resisted. It would be better to submit."

sentences.zh: 天錫怒，貶皓為宣威護軍。

translations.literal: Tiansun was angry and demoted Hao to Protector General Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansun was enraged and demoted Hao to Protector General Who Displays Might.

sentences.zh: 廣武太守辛章曰：「馬建出於行陳，必不為國家用。」

translations.literal: Xin Zhang, Administrator of Guangwu, said: "Ma Jian rose from the ranks — he will surely not serve the state's interests."
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zhang, Administrator of Guangwu, said, "Ma Jian rose from the ranks. He will never serve the state's true interests."

sentences.zh: 苟萇使姚萇帥甲士三千為前驅。

translations.literal: Gou Chang sent Yao Chang to lead three thousand armored soldiers as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Chang sent Yao Chang ahead with three thousand armored soldiers as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，馬建帥萬人迎降，餘兵皆散走。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Ma Jian led ten thousand men forward to surrender; the remaining troops all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Ma Jian came forward with ten thousand men and surrendered; the rest of his force scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，苟萇及掌據戰於洪池，據兵敗，馬為亂兵所殺，其屬董儒授之以馬，據曰：「吾三督諸軍，再秉節鉞，八將禁旅，十總外兵，寵任極矣。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Gou Chang and Zhang Ju fought at Hongchi; Ju's army was defeated, and his horse was killed by disorderly troops. His follower Dong Ru offered him a horse. Ju said: "I have thrice supervised the armies, twice held the imperial baton, commanded eight generals of the palace guard, and ten times overseen external troops — favor and trust could go no further.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Gou Chang and Zhang Ju fought at Hongchi. Ju's army was routed, and his horse was killed in the chaos. His follower Dong Ru offered him another mount. Ju said, "I have thrice commanded the armies, twice borne the imperial baton, led eight generals of the palace guard, and ten times overseen field armies. Honor and trust could go no higher.

sentences.zh: 今卒困於此，此吾之死地也，尚安之乎！」

translations.literal: Now at last I am trapped here — this is my place of death; how could I seek safety!"
translations.idiomatic: Now I am trapped here at last. This is where I die. How could I seek safety?"

sentences.zh: 乃就帳免冑，西向稽首，伏劍而死。

translations.literal: He then went to his tent, removed his helmet, bowed to the west, and fell on his sword and died.
translations.idiomatic: He went to his tent, removed his helmet, bowed to the west, and fell on his sword.

sentences.zh: 秦兵殺軍司席仂。

translations.literal: Qin troops killed Army Director Xi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Qin troops killed Army Director Xi Le.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，秦兵入清塞，天錫遣司兵趙充哲帥眾拒之。

translations.literal: On guisi, Qin troops entered Qingsai; Tiansun sent Arms Officer Zhao Chongzhe to command the force resisting them.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Qin forces entered Qingsai. Tiansun sent Arms Officer Zhao Chongzhe to lead the resistance.

sentences.zh: 秦兵與充哲戰於赤岸，大破之，俘斬三萬八千級，充哲死。

translations.literal: Qin troops fought Chongzhe at Chian, routed him utterly, captured and killed thirty-eight thousand men, and Chongzhe died.
translations.idiomatic: Qin forces met Chongzhe at Chian and routed him, capturing or killing thirty-eight thousand men. Chongzhe was killed.

sentences.zh: 天錫出城自戰，城內又叛。

translations.literal: Tiansun went out of the city to fight in person, and within the city there was rebellion as well.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansun rode out to fight in person, even as rebellion broke out inside the city.

sentences.zh: 天錫與數千騎奔還姑臧。

translations.literal: Tiansun fled back to Guzang with several thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansun fled back to Guzang with a few thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 甲午，秦兵至姑臧，天錫素車白馬，面縛輿櫬，降於軍門。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Qin troops reached Guzang; Tiansun came in an unadorned cart with a white horse, his face bound and a coffin borne before him, and surrendered at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Qin troops reached Guzang. Tiansun came in a plain cart drawn by a white horse, his face bound and a coffin carried before him, and surrendered at the army gate.

sentences.zh: 苟萇釋縛焚梓，送於長安。

translations.literal: Gou Chang released his bonds, burned the coffin, and sent him to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Chang freed him, burned the coffin, and sent him on to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 涼州郡縣悉降於秦。

translations.literal: All commanderies and counties of Liangzhou submitted to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Every commandery and county in Liangzhou submitted to Qin.

sentences.zh: 九月，秦王堅以梁熙為涼州刺史，鎮姑臧。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, King Fu Jian of Qin appointed Liang Xi Inspector of Liangzhou and stationed him at Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, King Fu Jian of Qin made Liang Xi Inspector of Liangzhou and posted him at Guzang.

sentences.zh: 徙豪右七千餘戶於關中，餘皆按堵如故。

translations.literal: More than seven thousand households of powerful families were relocated to Guanzhong; the rest were all settled in peace as before.
translations.idiomatic: More than seven thousand households of the local elite were moved to Guanzhong; the rest were left undisturbed in their homes.

sentences.zh: 封天錫為歸義侯，拜北部尚書。

translations.literal: Tiansun was enfeoffed as Marquis of Returning Allegiance and appointed Northern Department Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansun was enfeoffed as Marquis of Returning Allegiance and appointed Northern Department Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 初，秦兵之出也，先為天錫築第於長安，至則居之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qin troops set out, a residence had already been built for Tiansun in Chang'an; when he arrived, he took up residence there.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Qin army even marched, a residence had been built for Tiansun in Chang'an. When he arrived, he moved in at once.

sentences.zh: 以天錫晉興太守隴西彭和正為黃門侍郎，治中從事武興蘇膺、敦煌太守張烈為尚書郎，西平太守金城趙凝為金城太守，高昌楊干為高昌太守；

translations.literal: Peng Hezheng of Longxi, Administrator of Jinxing under Tiansun, was made Palace Attendant; Su Ying of Wuxing, Administrative Aide, and Zhang Lie, Administrator of Dunhuang, were made Masters of Writing; Zhao Ning of Jincheng, Administrator of Xiping, was made Administrator of Jincheng; Yang Gan was made Administrator of Gaochang;
translations.idiomatic: Peng Hezheng of Longxi, Tiansun's Administrator of Jinxing, was made Palace Attendant; Su Ying of Wuxing, Administrative Aide, and Zhang Lie, Administrator of Dunhuang, were made Masters of Writing; Zhao Ning of Jincheng, Administrator of Xiping, was confirmed as Administrator of Jincheng; and Yang Gan was made Administrator of Gaochang;

sentences.zh: 餘皆隨才擢敘。

translations.literal: the rest were all promoted and assigned according to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: the rest were promoted and assigned according to their abilities.

sentences.zh: 梁熙清儉愛民，河右安之，以天錫武威太守敦煌索泮為別駕，宋皓為主簿。

translations.literal: Liang Xi was upright, frugal, and loved the people; the lands west of the Yellow River were settled under him. He made Suo Pan of Dunhuang, Administrator of Wuwei under Tiansun, Administrative Aide, and Song Hao Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi governed with integrity and frugality and cared for the people, bringing peace to the lands west of the Yellow River. He made Suo Pan of Dunhuang, Tiansun's former Administrator of Wuwei, his Administrative Aide, and Song Hao his Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 西平郭護起兵攻秦，熙以皓為折衝將軍，討平之。

translations.literal: Guo Hu of Xiping raised troops to attack Qin; Xi made Hao General Who Breaks the Charge and suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Hu of Xiping raised troops against Qin. Xi made Hao General Who Breaks the Charge and put down the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 桓沖聞秦攻涼州，遣兗州刺史朱序、江州刺史桓石秀與荊州督護桓羆遊軍沔、漢，為涼州聲援；

translations.literal: When Huan Chong heard that Qin was attacking Liangzhou, he sent Zhu Xu, Inspector of Yanzhou; Huan Shixiu, Inspector of Jiangzhou; and Huan Pi, Protector of Jingzhou, to lead mobile forces along the Han and Mian rivers as a supporting demonstration for Liangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Chong learned that Qin was attacking Liangzhou, he sent Zhu Xu, Inspector of Yanzhou; Huan Shixiu, Inspector of Jiangzhou; and Huan Pi, Protector of Jingzhou, to lead mobile columns along the Han and Mian rivers in a show of support for Liangzhou;

sentences.zh: 又遣豫州刺史桓伊帥眾向壽陽，淮南太守劉波泛舟淮、泗，欲橈秦以救涼。

translations.literal: he further sent Huan Yi, Inspector of Yuzhou, to lead troops toward Shouyang, and Liu Bo, Administrator of Huainan, to sail the Huai and Si rivers, intending to harass Qin to rescue Liang.
translations.idiomatic: he also sent Huan Yi, Inspector of Yuzhou, toward Shouyang and Liu Bo, Administrator of Huainan, to sail the Huai and Si rivers, hoping to harass Qin and relieve Liang.

sentences.zh: 聞涼州敗沒，皆罷兵。

translations.literal: When they heard that Liangzhou had been defeated and lost, they all disbanded their troops.
translations.idiomatic: When they learned that Liangzhou had fallen, they all withdrew their forces.

sentences.zh: 初，哀帝減田租，畝收二升。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Ai had reduced the field tax to two sheng per mu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Ai had reduced the land tax to two sheng per mu.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，除度田收租之制，王公以下，口稅米三斛，蠲在役之身。

translations.literal: On yisi, the system of surveying fields and collecting rent was abolished; from kings and dukes downward, a head tax of three hu of grain was levied, and those performing corvée labor were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, the field-survey land tax was abolished. From kings and dukes downward, each person owed three hu of grain, while those performing corvée were exempt.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，移淮北民於准南。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the people north of the Huai were relocated south of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the people north of the Huai were resettled south of the river.

sentences.zh: 劉衛辰為代所逼，求救於秦，秦王堅以幽州刺史行唐公洛為北討大都督，帥幽、冀兵十萬擊代；

translations.literal: Liu Weichen, pressed by Dai, sought rescue from Qin; King Fu Jian of Qin made Duke Luo of Xingtang, Inspector of Youzhou, Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign and sent one hundred thousand troops from You and Ji to attack Dai;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weichen, hard pressed by Dai, appealed to Qin for help. King Fu Jian of Qin made Duke Luo of Xingtang, Inspector of Youzhou, Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign and sent one hundred thousand troops from You and Ji against Dai;

sentences.zh: 使并州刺史俱難、鎮軍將軍鄧羌、尚書趙遷、李柔、前將軍朱肜、前禁將軍張蚝、右禁將軍郭慶帥步騎二十萬，東出和龍，西出上都，皆與洛會，以衛辰為鄉導。

translations.literal: he sent Ju Nan, Inspector of Bingzhou; Deng Qiang, General Who Stabilizes the Army; Masters of Writing Zhao Qian and Li Rou; Zhu Rong, Forward General; Zhang Hao, Forward Guard General; and Guo Qing, Right Guard General, to lead two hundred thousand infantry and cavalry east from Helong and west from Shangdu, all to join Luo, with Weichen as guide.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Ju Nan, Inspector of Bingzhou; Deng Qiang, General Who Stabilizes the Army; Masters of Writing Zhao Qian and Li Rou; Zhu Rong, Forward General; Zhang Hao, Forward Guard General; and Guo Qing, Right Guard General, with two hundred thousand infantry and cavalry east from Helong and west from Shangdu to join Luo, using Weichen as their guide.

sentences.zh: 洛，菁之弟也。

translations.literal: Luo was Jing's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Luo was Fu Jian's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 苟萇之伐涼州也，遣揚武將軍馬暉、建武將軍杜周帥八千騎西出恩宿，邀張天錫走路，期會姑臧。

translations.literal: When Gou Chang attacked Liangzhou, he sent Yangwu General Ma Hui and Jianwu General Du Zhou to lead eight thousand cavalry west from Ensu to intercept Zhang Tiansun's escape route, with orders to rendezvous at Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: During Gou Chang's campaign against Liangzhou, he sent Yangwu General Ma Hui and Jianwu General Du Zhou with eight thousand cavalry west from Ensu to cut off Zhang Tiansun's escape and rendezvous at Guzang.

sentences.zh: 暉等行澤中，值水失期，於法應斬，有司奏徵下獄。

translations.literal: Hui and the others traveled through marshes, encountered water, and missed the deadline; by law they should be beheaded, and the responsible officials memorialized to summon and imprison them.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and his men crossed marshland, ran into flooding, and missed their deadline. By military law they deserved execution, and the responsible officials memorialized to have them recalled and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅曰：「水春冬耗竭。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin said: "Water is exhausted in spring and winter.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin said, "Water runs low in spring and winter.

sentences.zh: 秋夏盛漲，此乃苟萇量事失宜，非暉等罪。

translations.literal: In autumn and summer it swells greatly — this was Gou Chang's failure to measure affairs properly, not the fault of Hui and the others.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn and summer it rises in flood. Gou Chang misjudged the conditions; this is not Hui's fault.

sentences.zh: 今天下方有事，宜宥過責功。

translations.literal: Now the realm is still unsettled — faults should be pardoned and merit demanded.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still at war. Pardon faults and demand merit instead.

sentences.zh: 命暉等回赴北軍，擊索虜以自贖。」

translations.literal: He ordered Hui and the others to return and join the northern army, attacking the Suo barbarians to redeem themselves."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Hui and his men to rejoin the northern army and strike the Suo tribes to redeem themselves."

sentences.zh: 眾咸以為萬里召將，非所以應速。

translations.literal: All thought that summoning generals from ten thousand li was not the way to respond quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Many argued that recalling generals from a thousand miles away was no way to meet an urgent need.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「暉等喜於免死，不可以常事疑也。」

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "Hui and the others rejoice at escaping death — one cannot suspect them as in ordinary affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "Hui and his men are grateful to have escaped death. You cannot judge them by ordinary standards."

sentences.zh: 暉等果倍道疾驅，遂及東軍。

translations.literal: Hui and the others indeed traveled by double marches at full speed and thus caught up with the eastern army.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and his men did indeed force double marches at full speed and caught up with the eastern army.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day of the month (jisi), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on New Year's Day, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 代王什翼犍使白部、獨孤部南御秦兵，皆不勝，又使南部大人劉庫仁將十萬騎御之。

translations.literal: King Shiyijian of Dai sent the Bai and Dugu tribes south to resist Qin troops; both were defeated. He then sent Liu Kuren, Southern Grand Chieftain, to command one hundred thousand cavalry to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: King Shiyijian of Dai sent the Bai and Dugu tribes south against Qin, but both were defeated. He then sent Liu Kuren, Southern Grand Chieftain, with one hundred thousand cavalry to hold them off.

sentences.zh: 庫仁者，衛辰之族，什翼犍之甥也，與秦兵戰於石子嶺，庫仁大敗。

translations.literal: Kuren was of Weichen's clan and Shiyijian's nephew by marriage; he fought Qin troops at Shizi Ridge and was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Kuren was a kinsman of Weichen and Shiyijian's nephew by marriage. He met Qin at Shizi Ridge and was routed.

sentences.zh: 什翼犍病，不能自將，乃帥諸部奔陰山之北。

translations.literal: Shiyijian was ill and could not command in person; he then led the various tribes north of Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyijian was ill and could not take the field himself, so he led the tribes north of the Yin Mountains.

sentences.zh: 高車雜種盡叛，四面寇鈔，不得芻牧，什翼犍復渡漠南。

translations.literal: All the mixed Gaoche tribes rebelled; raiders attacked from every side, and pasture and fodder could not be obtained; Shiyijian crossed south of the desert again.
translations.idiomatic: The mixed Gaoche tribes all rose in revolt. Raiders closed in from every side, and there was no pasture or fodder to be had. Shiyijian crossed south of the desert once more.

sentences.zh: 聞秦兵稍退，十二月，什翼犍還雲中。

translations.literal: When he heard that Qin troops had gradually withdrawn, in the twelfth month Shiyijian returned to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Qin forces were gradually withdrawing, Shiyijian returned to Yunzhong in the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 初，什翼犍分國之半以授弟孤，孤卒，子斤失職怨望。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shiyijian had granted half the state to his younger brother Gu; when Gu died, his son Jin lost his position and harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shiyijian had given half the realm to his younger brother Gu. When Gu died, his son Jin lost his standing and nursed a grievance.

sentences.zh: 世子寔及弟翰早卒，寔子珪尚幼，慕容妃之子閼婆、壽鳩、紇根、地干、力真、窟咄皆長，繼嗣未定。

translations.literal: The heir apparent Shi and his younger brother Han had both died early; Shi's son Gui was still young, while the sons of Lady Murong — Ebo, Shoujiu, Heggen, Digan, Lizhen, and Kudu — were all grown, and the succession was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent Shi and his brother Han had both died young. Shi's son Gui was still a child, while Lady Murong's sons — Ebo, Shoujiu, Heggen, Digan, Lizhen, and Kudu — were all grown men, and the succession remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 時秦兵尚在君子津，諸子每夜執兵警衛。

translations.literal: At this time Qin troops were still at Junzi Ford; each night the princes took up arms to stand guard.
translations.idiomatic: Qin troops were still at Junzi Ford, and each night the princes took up arms to stand guard.

sentences.zh: 斤因說什翼犍之庶長子寔君曰：「王將立慕容妃之子，欲先殺汝，故頃來諸子每夜戎服，以兵繞廬帳，伺便將發耳。」

translations.literal: Jin therefore said to Shijun, Shiyijian's eldest son by a concubine: "The King intends to establish Lady Murong's son and wishes first to kill you; that is why lately each night the princes wear armor and surround the tent with weapons, waiting for an opportunity to strike."
translations.idiomatic: Jin therefore said to Shijun, Shiyijian's eldest son by a concubine, "The King means to install one of Lady Murong's sons and plans to kill you first. That is why the princes have been wearing armor each night and circling the tent with weapons, waiting for their chance to strike."

sentences.zh: 寔君信之，遂殺諸弟，並弒什翼犍。

translations.literal: Shijun believed him, then killed his younger brothers and also assassinated Shiyijian.
translations.idiomatic: Shijun believed him, killed his younger brothers, and assassinated Shiyijian.

sentences.zh: 是夜，諸子婦及部人奔告秦軍，秦李柔、張蚝勒兵趨雲中；

translations.literal: That same night, the princes' wives and tribesmen fled to inform the Qin army; Li Rou and Zhang Hao of Qin led troops in haste toward Yunzhong;
translations.idiomatic: That same night, the princes' wives and tribesmen fled to warn the Qin army. Li Rou and Zhang Hao of Qin marched at once on Yunzhong;

sentences.zh: 部眾逃潰，國中大亂。

translations.literal: the tribesmen scattered in flight and the state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: the tribesmen scattered, and the realm descended into chaos.

sentences.zh: 珪母賀氏以珪走依賀訥。

translations.literal: Gui's mother, Lady He, fled with Gui to take refuge with He Ne.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's mother, Lady He, fled with the boy to seek refuge with He Ne.

sentences.zh: 訥，野干之子也。

translations.literal: Ne was the son of Yegan.
translations.idiomatic: Ne was the son of Yegan.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅召代長史燕鳳，問代所以亂故，鳳具以狀對。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin summoned Yan Feng, Chief Clerk of Dai, inquired into the reasons for Dai's disorder, and Feng reported the full circumstances in detail.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin summoned Yan Feng, formerly Dai's chief clerk, and asked what had plunged the realm into chaos. Feng laid out the whole affair in detail.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「天下之惡一也。」

translations.literal: Jian said: "Evil under Heaven is one."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "Wickedness under Heaven knows no distinction."

sentences.zh: 乃執寔君及斤，至長安，車裂之。

translations.literal: He then seized Shijun and Jin, brought them to Chang'an, and had them torn apart by chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He had Shijun and Jin seized, brought to Chang'an, and torn apart by chariots.

sentences.zh: 堅欲遷珪於長安，鳳固請曰：「代王初亡，群下叛散，遺孫沖幼，莫相統攝。

translations.literal: Jian wished to move Gui to Chang'an; Feng earnestly pleaded, saying: "The King of Dai has newly perished; his followers have rebelled and scattered; his surviving grandson Chong is young, and none can lead and govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian intended to transfer Gui to Chang'an, but Feng urgently petitioned: "The King of Dai has only just died. His followers have splintered in revolt, his grandson Chong is still a child, and no one stands ready to hold the tribes together.

sentences.zh: 其別部大人劉庫仁，勇而有智；

translations.literal: Liu Kuren, Grand Chieftain of a separate division, is brave and wise;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuren, a grand chieftain of one branch, is brave and shrewd;

sentences.zh: 鐵弗衛辰，狡猾多變，皆不可獨任。

translations.literal: Tiefe Weichen is cunning and changeable; neither may be entrusted alone.
translations.idiomatic: Tiefe Weichen is devious and unstable. Neither man should be trusted with sole authority.

sentences.zh: 宜分諸部為二，令此兩人統之；

translations.literal: It is fitting to divide the tribes into two and have these two men command them;
translations.idiomatic: The tribes should be split in two, with these two men placed in command of each half;

sentences.zh: 兩人素有深仇，其勢莫敢先發。

translations.literal: the two have long borne a deep grudge, and in such a situation neither will dare strike first.
translations.idiomatic: the two have nursed a deep feud for years, and neither will dare strike first against the other.

sentences.zh: 俟其孫稍長，引而立之，是陛下有存亡繼絕之德於代，使其子子孫孫永為不侵不叛之臣，此安邊之良策也。」

translations.literal: When his grandson grows somewhat older, bring him forward and install him — then Your Majesty will have the virtue of preserving what was perishing and continuing what was cut off for Dai, causing sons and sons' sons forever to be subjects who neither invade nor rebel; this is an excellent policy for securing the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: When the boy grows older, install him as ruler. Your Majesty will have shown the virtue of saving a line on the brink of extinction, and Dai's heirs will forever remain loyal subjects who never raid or rebel. It is the surest way to secure the border."

sentences.zh: 堅從之，分代民為二部，自河以東屬庫仁，自河以西屬衛辰，各拜官爵，使統其眾。

translations.literal: Jian followed this advice, divided the people of Dai into two divisions — east of the river under Kuren, west of the river under Weichen — invested each with rank and title, and had them command their respective followers.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian agreed. He split the Dai tribes in two: Kuren governed those east of the river, Weichen those west. Each received an official rank and title and command over his people.

sentences.zh: 賀氏以珪歸獨孤部，與南部大人長孫嵩、元佗等皆依庫仁。

translations.literal: Lady He took Gui back to the Dugu tribe; she, Southern Grand Chieftain Changsun Song, Yuan Tuo, and others all attached themselves to Kuren.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He brought Gui to the Dugu tribe. She, along with Southern Grand Chieftain Changsun Song, Yuan Tuo, and others, all threw in their lot with Kuren.

sentences.zh: 行唐公洛以什翼犍子窟咄年長，遷之長安。

translations.literal: Duke Luo of Xingtang, because Shiyijian's son Kudu was grown, transferred him to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Luo of Xingtang, noting that Shiyijian's son Kudu had come of age, had him moved to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 堅使窟咄入太學讀書。

translations.literal: Jian had Kudu enter the Imperial Academy to study.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent Kudu to the Imperial Academy to receive an education.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「張天錫承祖父之資，藉百年之業，擅命河右，叛換偏隅。

translations.literal: An edict was issued saying: "Zhang Tiansun relied on his grandfather's resources and borrowed a century of achievement, arrogating authority west of the Yellow River and rebelling in a distant corner.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued an edict: "Zhang Tiansun drew on his grandfather's legacy and a century of power built up in his family, claiming independent rule west of the Yellow River and revolting in a distant corner of the realm.

sentences.zh: 索頭世跨朔北，中分區域，東賓穢貊，西引烏孫，控弦百萬，虎視雲中。

translations.literal: The Suotou for generations straddled the northern frontier, holding the central region; to the east they received the Huimo as subjects, to the west they drew in the Wusun; they commanded a million bowmen and glared like tigers at Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Suotou Xianbei had for generations dominated the north, commanding the heartland: they brought the Huimo into their fold in the east, the Wusun in the west, fielded a million archers, and fixed a tiger's glare on Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 爰命兩師，分討黠虜，役不淹歲，窮殄二凶，俘降百萬，闢土九千，五帝之所未賓，周、漢之所未至，莫不重譯來王，懷風率職。

translations.literal: Therefore two armies were ordered to march separately against the cunning barbarians; the campaign did not exceed a year, both villains were utterly destroyed, a million captives submitted, nine thousand li of territory was opened — lands to which neither the Five Emperors nor the Zhou and Han had brought submission; none failed to send tribute through many interpreters, come to pay court bearing the winds of loyalty, and fulfill their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Two armies were dispatched to subdue these crafty foes. In less than a year both enemies were destroyed, a million captives surrendered, and nine thousand li of land were brought under rule — territory that neither the Five Emperors nor the Zhou and Han had ever reached. Peoples from the farthest corners sent tribute through layers of interpreters, came to court in homage, and pledged their service.

sentences.zh: 有司可速班功受爵，戎士悉復之五歲，賜爵三級。」

translations.literal: The relevant offices may promptly award merit and confer ranks; all soldiers are to be exempt from corvée for five years and granted three ranks of nobility."
translations.idiomatic: Let the offices promptly distribute rewards and confer nobility. All soldiers shall be exempt from corvée for five years and receive three ranks of nobility."

sentences.zh: 於是加行唐公洛征西將軍，以鄧羌為并州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Duke Luo of Xingtang was promoted to General Who Conquers the West, and Deng Qiang was made Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Luo of Xingtang was then made General Who Conquers the West, and Deng Qiang was appointed Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 陽平國常侍慕容紹私謂其兄楷曰：「秦恃其強大，務勝不休，北戍雲中，南守蜀、漢，轉運萬里，道殣相望。

translations.literal: Murong Shao, Attendant-in-Ordinary of Yangping, privately said to his elder brother Kai: "Qin relies on its strength, striving for victory without cease — garrisoning Yunzhong in the north, holding Shu and Han in the south; transport extends ten thousand li, and corpses litter the roads one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shao, Attendant-in-Ordinary of Yangping, took his elder brother Kai aside and said, "Qin counts on its might and will not stop until it has won everything — garrisoning Yunzhong in the north, holding Shu and Han in the south. Supply lines stretch ten thousand li, and the dead lie along every road.

sentences.zh: 兵疲於外，民困於內，危亡近矣。

translations.literal: The armies weary abroad, the people suffer within — ruin is near.
translations.idiomatic: The armies are exhausted abroad and the people worn down at home. Collapse cannot be far off.

sentences.zh: 冠軍叔仁智度英拔，必能恢復燕祚，吾屬但當愛身以待時耳！」

translations.literal: Champion General Shuren is wise and outstanding in talent; he will surely be able to restore Yan's royal fortune. We need only preserve ourselves and await the hour!"
translations.idiomatic: Champion General Shuren possesses rare intelligence and talent — he is sure to restore the House of Yan. All we need do is keep ourselves safe and wait for the right moment!"

sentences.zh: 初，秦人既克涼州，議討西障氐、羌。

translations.literal: Earlier, once the people of Qin had taken Liangzhou, they debated attacking the Di and Qiang of the western frontier.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin captured Liangzhou, the court debated whether to subjugate the Di and Qiang of the western marches.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅曰：「彼種落雜居，不相統壹，不能為中國大患。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin said: "Those tribes live mixed together without unified leadership; they cannot become a great calamity to the Central States.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian of Qin said, "Those peoples live intermingled without a single leader. They pose no serious threat to the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 宜先撫諭，徵其租稅。

translations.literal: It is fitting first to soothe and instruct them and collect their taxes and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: We should first win them over with kindness and collect taxes and tribute from them.

sentences.zh: 若不從命，然後討之。」

translations.literal: If they do not obey, then afterward attack them."
translations.idiomatic: Only if they defy us should we turn to force."

sentences.zh: 乃使殿中將軍張旬前行宣慰，庭中將軍魏曷飛帥騎二萬七千隨之。

translations.literal: He then sent Palace General Zhang Xun ahead to proclaim reassurance, with Court General Wei Yifei leading twenty-seven thousand cavalry following after.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Palace General Zhang Xun ahead to proclaim the court's reassurance, with Court General Wei Yifei and twenty-seven thousand cavalry in support.

sentences.zh: 曷飛忿其恃險不服，縱兵擊之，大掠而歸。

translations.literal: Yifei resented that they relied on rough terrain and refused submission; he unleashed his troops to attack them, looted heavily, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yifei, angry that they relied on rugged terrain to defy the court, attacked without restraint, plundered extensively, and marched back.

sentences.zh: 堅怒其違命，鞭之二百，斬前鋒督護儲安以謝氐、羌。

translations.literal: Jian was angry at his disobedience, had him flogged two hundred strokes, and executed Forward Commander Chu An to apologize to the Di and Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian, furious at this disobedience, had Yifei flogged two hundred times and executed Forward Commander Chu An as an apology to the Di and Qiang.

sentences.zh: 氐、羌大悅，降附貢獻者八萬三千餘落。

translations.literal: The Di and Qiang were greatly pleased; those who submitted and offered tribute numbered more than eighty-three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The Di and Qiang were greatly pleased. More than eighty-three thousand clans submitted and sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 雍州士族先因亂流寓河西者，皆聽還本。

translations.literal: Gentry clans of Yongzhou who had earlier, on account of turmoil, drifted into exile west of the Yellow River were all permitted to return to their native places.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry families of Yongzhou who had fled the turmoil to settle west of the river were all permitted to return home.

sentences.zh: 劉庫仁分招撫離散，恩信甚著，奉事拓跋珪恩勤周備，不以廢興易意，常謂諸子曰：「此兒有高天下之志，必能恢隆祖業，汝曹當謹遇之。」

translations.literal: Liu Kuren separately summoned and soothed those scattered in flight; his kindness and trustworthiness were highly renowned. In serving Tuoba Gui he was devoted and thorough in every respect, never shifting his loyalty according to fortune or decline. He often told his sons: "This child has ambition to reach high under Heaven; he will surely be able to restore and exalt the ancestral enterprise. You must treat him with care."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuren rallied and comforted those scattered by the chaos, earning wide renown for his loyalty and generosity. He served Tuoba Gui with tireless devotion, never wavering whether the house was rising or falling. He often told his sons, "This boy has the ambition to rule the world. He will restore the ancestral patrimony. Treat him with the utmost respect."

sentences.zh: 秦王堅賞其功，加廣武將軍，給幢麾鼓蓋。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin rewarded his achievement, promoted him to General of Guangwu, and granted him banner, staff, drum, and canopy.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian rewarded his service, made him General of Guangwu, and granted him the full trappings of command — banner, staff, drum, and canopy.

sentences.zh: 劉衛辰恥在庫仁之下，怒，殺秦五原太守而叛。

translations.literal: Liu Weichen was shamed at ranking below Kuren; in anger he killed Qin's Administrator of Wuyuan and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weichen, humiliated at serving under Kuren, flew into a rage, killed Qin's Administrator of Wuyuan, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 庫仁擊衛辰，破之，追至陰山西北千餘里，獲其妻子。

translations.literal: Kuren attacked Weichen, defeated him, pursued him more than a thousand li northwest of Yinshan, and captured his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Kuren attacked Weichen, routed him, and pursued him more than a thousand li beyond the northwest of the Yin Mountains, capturing his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 又西擊庫狄部，徙其部落，置之桑干川。

translations.literal: He also attacked the Kudi tribe in the west, relocated their encampments, and settled them on the Sanggan River.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked the Kudi tribe in the west, relocated their people, and resettled them on the Sanggan River.

sentences.zh: 久之，堅以衛辰為西單于，督攝河西雜類，屯代來城。

translations.literal: After some time, Jian made Weichen Western Chanyu, supervisor of the mixed peoples west of the Yellow River, garrisoning Dailai City.
translations.idiomatic: In time, Fu Jian appointed Weichen Western Chanyu, placing him over the mixed tribes west of the river with a garrison at Dailai City.

sentences.zh: 是歲，乞伏司繁卒，子國仁立。

translations.literal: That year, Qifu Sifan died, and his son Guoren succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qifu Sifan died, and his son Guoren succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝上之中太元二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — second year of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — second year of Taiyuan (

sentences.zh: 丁丑，公元三七七年）

translations.literal: dingchou, corresponding to 377 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingchou year, 377 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，高句麗、新羅、西南夷皆遣使入貢於秦。

translations.literal: In spring, Goguryeo, Silla, and the southwestern Yi all sent envoys to offer tribute to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, Goguryeo, Silla, and the tribes of the southwest all sent envoys to pay tribute to Qin.

sentences.zh: 趙故將作功曹熊邈屢為秦王堅言石氏宮室器玩之盛，堅以邈為將作長史，領尚方丞，大修舟艦、兵器，飾以金銀，頗極精巧。

translations.literal: Xiong Miao, former Master of Works Clerk of Zhao, repeatedly told King Fu Jian of Qin of the magnificence of the Shi clan's palaces and precious objects. Jian made Miao Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Works, concurrently Director of the Imperial Workshops, and undertook great repairs of ships and weapons, adorned with gold and silver, to an extreme of refinement and ingenuity.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Miao, formerly a clerk in Zhao's directorate of works, repeatedly regaled King Fu Jian with accounts of the splendor of the Shi family's palaces and treasures. Fu Jian appointed him chief clerk of the directorate of works and director of the imperial workshops, and launched a lavish program to build ships and weapons adorned with gold and silver to the highest degree of craftsmanship.

sentences.zh: 慕容農私言於慕容垂曰：「自王猛之死，秦之法制，日以頹靡，今又重之以奢侈，殃將至矣，圖讖之言，行當有驗。

translations.literal: Murong Nong privately said to Murong Chui: "Since Wang Meng's death, Qin's laws and institutions have daily declined and lapsed; now extravagance is added on top — calamity will soon arrive. The words of prophetic charts will before long be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong took Murong Chui aside and said, "Since Wang Meng died, Qin's laws have crumbled day by day. Now extravagance is piled on decay — disaster cannot be far off. The prophecies will soon come true.

sentences.zh: 大王宜結納英傑以承天意，時不可失也！」

translations.literal: Great King, you ought to gather and win over heroes and outstanding men to accord with Heaven's intent — the moment must not be lost!"
translations.idiomatic: My lord should gather the realm's finest men to seize Heaven's mandate. The moment will not wait!"

sentences.zh: 垂笑曰：「天下事非爾所及。」

translations.literal: Chui smiled and said: "Affairs under Heaven are not for you to reach."
translations.idiomatic: Chui smiled and said, "Matters of the realm are beyond your ken."

sentences.zh: 桓豁表兗州刺史朱序為梁州刺史，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Huan Huo memorialized that Zhu Xu, Inspector of Yanzhou, be made Inspector of Liangzhou and stationed at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Huo recommended that Zhu Xu, Inspector of Yanzhou, be appointed Inspector of Liangzhou and stationed at Xiangyang to hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁未，以尚書僕射謝安為司徒，安讓不拜；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingwei, Xie An, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Minister over the Masses; An declined and did not accept;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingwei, Xie An, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed Minister over the Masses, but he declined the post;

sentences.zh: 復加侍中、都督揚、豫、徐、兗、青五州諸軍事。

translations.literal: he was again given the additional posts of Palace Attendant and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the five provinces of Yang, Yu, Xu, Yan, and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: and was instead given the additional titles of Palace Attendant and Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in the five provinces of Yang, Yu, Xu, Yan, and Qing.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，征西大將軍、荊州刺史桓豁卒。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Huan Huo, General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Huan Huo — General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Jingzhou — passed away.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛丑，以桓沖都督江、荊、梁、益、寧、交、廣七州諸軍事，領荊州刺史；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinchou, Huan Chong was made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the seven provinces of Jiang, Jing, Liang, Yi, Ning, Jiao, and Guang, and concurrently Inspector of Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on xinchou, Huan Chong was made Commander-in-Chief over military affairs in Jiang, Jing, Liang, Yi, Ning, Jiao, and Guang, and appointed Inspector of Jingzhou;

sentences.zh: 以沖子嗣為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Chong's son Si was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Si was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以五兵尚書王蘊都督江南諸軍事，假節，領徐州刺史；

translations.literal: Also, Wang Yun, Minister of the Five Armies, was made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs south of the Yangzi, granted the credential staff, and made Inspector of Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun, Minister of the Five Armies, was made Commander-in-Chief south of the Yangzi, granted the credential staff, and appointed Inspector of Xuzhou;

sentences.zh: 征西司馬領南郡相謝玄為兗州刺史，領廣陵相，監江北諸軍事。

translations.literal: Xie Xuan, Western Expedition Marshal concurrently Administrator of Nan Commandery, was made Inspector of Yanzhou and concurrently Administrator of Guangling, overseeing all military affairs north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan, Western Expedition Marshal and Administrator of Nan Commandery, was appointed Inspector of Yanzhou and Administrator of Guangling, with oversight of all military affairs north of the river.

sentences.zh: 桓沖以秦人強盛，欲移阻江南，奏自江陵徙鎮上明，使冠軍將軍劉波守江陵，咨議參軍楊亮守江夏。

translations.literal: Huan Chong, because the people of Qin were powerful and flourishing, wished to shift his defensive barrier south of the Yangzi; he memorialized to move his headquarters from Jiangling to Shangming, sent Champion General Liu Bo to hold Jiangling, and Staff Advisor Yang Liang to hold Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Qin's growing might, Huan Chong sought to pull Jin's defenses back south of the Yangzi. He petitioned to move his headquarters from Jiangling to Shangming, leaving Champion General Liu Bo at Jiangling and Staff Advisor Yang Liang at Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 王蘊固讓徐州，謝安曰：「卿居后父之重，不應妄自菲薄，以虧時遇。」

translations.literal: Wang Yun firmly declined Xuzhou; Xie An said: "You occupy the weighty position of the Empress's father; you ought not rashly belittle yourself and thus fall short of the opportunity of the times."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun firmly refused Xuzhou. Xie An told him, "As the Empress's father, you hold a position of great weight. You must not sell yourself short and squander this moment."

sentences.zh: 蘊乃受命。

translations.literal: Yun then accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun accepted the post.

sentences.zh: 初，中書郎郗超自以其父愔位遇應在謝安之右，而安入掌機權，愔優遊散地，常憤邑形於辭色，由是與謝氏有隙。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chi Chao, Palace Scribe, considered that his father Kai's rank and treatment ought to be above Xie An's, yet An entered to wield decisive power while Kai dwelt at leisure in an unfilled post; Kai often showed resentment in word and countenance — hence a rift with the Xie clan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chi Chao, a palace scribe, believed his father Chi Kai deserved higher standing than Xie An. Yet Xie An had seized real power while Kai languished in an idle post. Resentment showed plainly on Kai's face and in his words, and a rift opened between the Chi and Xie clans.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷方以秦寇為憂，詔求文武良將可以鎮御北方者，謝安以兄子玄應詔。

translations.literal: At this time the court was just then anxious about Qin invaders; an edict sought civil and military men of quality who could garrison and defend the north. Xie An responded to the edict with his nephew Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then preoccupied with the Qin threat and issued a call for able civil and military leaders who could hold the northern frontier. Xie An nominated his nephew Xuan.

sentences.zh: 超聞之，歎曰：「安之明，乃能違眾舉親；

translations.literal: When Chao heard this, he sighed and said: "An's wisdom — to be able to go against the crowd and elevate a kinsman;
translations.idiomatic: When Chi Chao heard of this, he sighed and said, "Xie An is wise indeed — daring to nominate a relative against general opinion;

sentences.zh: 玄之才，足以不負所舉。」

translations.literal: Xuan's talent is sufficient not to fail what was recommended."
translations.idiomatic: and Xuan's talent is more than equal to the trust placed in him."

sentences.zh: 眾咸以為不然。

translations.literal: All the crowd considered this wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Most thought him mistaken.

sentences.zh: 超曰：「吾嘗與玄共在桓公府，見其使才，雖履屐間未嘗不得其任，是以知之。」

translations.literal: Chao said: "I once served together with Xuan in Duke Huan's mansion; I saw how he employed talent — even between slipper and mat he never failed to assign each man his proper task. That is how I know."
translations.idiomatic: Chi Chao said, "I served with Xuan in Duke Huan's household and watched how he used men. He never misplaced talent, even in the smallest assignment. That is how I know."

sentences.zh: 玄募驍勇之士，得彭城劉牢之等數人。

translations.literal: Xuan recruited fierce and brave men and obtained several, including Liu Laozhi of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan recruited bold fighters and won over several daring men, including Liu Laozhi of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 以牢之為參軍，常領精銳為前鋒，戰無不捷。

translations.literal: He made Laozhi a staff officer, regularly leading elite troops as vanguard; in battle there was none he did not win.
translations.idiomatic: He made Laozhi a staff officer and regularly led elite troops as vanguard. In every battle they prevailed.

sentences.zh: 時號「北府兵」，敵人畏之。

translations.literal: At the time they were called the "Northern Headquarters Troops"; enemies feared them.
translations.idiomatic: They became known as the Northern Headquarters Army, and their enemies feared them.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，護軍將軍、散騎常侍王彪之卒。

translations.literal: On renyin, Wang Biaozhi, Protector-General and Attendant-in-Ordinary at the Imperial Cadency, died.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Wang Biaozhi, Protector-General and Attendant-in-Ordinary, passed away.

sentences.zh: 初，謝安欲增修宮室，彪之曰：「中興之初，即東府為宮，殊為儉陋。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xie An wished to enlarge and repair the palace; Biaozhi said: "At the beginning of the Restoration, the Eastern Mansion served immediately as palace — it was exceptionally spare and crude.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xie An proposed expanding the palace, Biaozhi objected: "At the founding of the Eastern Jin, the Eastern Mansion was pressed into service as the palace — it was painfully bare and crude.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之亂，成帝止蘭台都坐，殆不蔽寒暑，是以更營新宮。

translations.literal: During Su Jun's rebellion, Emperor Cheng halted at the Lantai audience hall, barely sheltering from cold and heat — therefore a new palace was built.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Jun's revolt, Emperor Cheng took refuge in the Lantai hall, scarcely shielded from summer heat or winter cold. That is why a new palace was built.

sentences.zh: 比之漢、魏則為儉，比之初過江則為侈矣。

translations.literal: Compared with Han and Wei it was still frugal; compared with the first crossing of the Yangzi it was already extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: By Han and Wei standards it was still modest; by the standards of the first years after crossing the Yangzi, it was already lavish.

sentences.zh: 今寇敵方強，豈可大興功役，勞擾百姓邪！」

translations.literal: Now invaders and enemies are just then powerful — how can one launch great works and labor, troubling and harrying the people!"
translations.idiomatic: With enemy armies at our gates, how can we launch grand construction projects that exhaust and harass the people?"

sentences.zh: 安曰：「宮室弊陋，後世謂人無能。」

translations.literal: An said: "If the palace is dilapidated and crude, posterity will say its occupants were incapable."
translations.idiomatic: Xie An replied, "If the palace remains shabby, posterity will judge us incapable rulers."

sentences.zh: 彪之曰：「凡任天下之重者，當保國寧家，緝熙政事，乃以修室為能邪？」

translations.literal: Biaozhi said: "All who bear the heavy burden of the realm ought to preserve the state and settle the house, harmonizing and brightening government — and yet take building rooms as capacity?"
translations.idiomatic: Biaozhi retorted, "Those who bear the weight of empire should secure the realm, restore order, and govern well — not measure their worth by the grandeur of their halls!"

sentences.zh: 安不能奪其議，故終彪之之世，無所營造。

translations.literal: An could not overcome his argument; therefore throughout Biaozhi's lifetime nothing was constructed.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An could not counter him, and no construction took place for the rest of Biaozhi's life.

sentences.zh: 十二月，臨海太守郗超卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Chi Chao, Administrator of Linhai, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Chi Chao, Administrator of Linhai, died.

sentences.zh: 初，超黨於桓氏，以父愔忠於王室，不令知之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chao was partisan to the Huan clan, but because his father Kai was loyal to the royal house, he did not let Kai know.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Chao had sided with the Huan clan, but hid this from his father Kai, who was devoted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及病甚，出一箱書授門生曰：「公年尊，我死之後，若以哀惋害寢食者，可呈此箱；

translations.literal: When his illness grew grave, he brought out a chest of documents and gave it to a disciple, saying: "My lord is advanced in years; after my death, if grief and sorrow harm his sleep and food, you may present this chest;
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened, Chi Chao produced a chest of documents and handed it to a disciple, saying, "My father is old. If after my death grief robs him of sleep and appetite, show him this chest;

sentences.zh: 不爾，即焚之。」

translations.literal: if not, then burn it."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise burn it."

sentences.zh: 既而愔果哀惋成疾，門生呈箱，皆與桓溫往反密計。

translations.literal: Before long Kai indeed grieved into illness; the disciple presented the chest — all were secret plans exchanged back and forth with Huan Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Kai did grieve himself ill. The disciple showed him the chest: inside were secret letters exchanged with Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 愔大怒曰：「小子死已晚矣！」

translations.literal: Kai flew into a rage and said: "The whelp died too late!"
translations.idiomatic: Kai erupted in fury: "That wretch should have died long ago!"

sentences.zh: 遂不復哭。

translations.literal: He then wept no more.
translations.idiomatic: He never wept again.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝上之中太元三年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — third year of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — third year of Taiyuan (

sentences.zh: 戊寅，公元三七八年）

translations.literal: wuyin, corresponding to 378 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wuyin year, 378 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，乙巳，作新宮，帝移居會稽王邸。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on yisi, the new palace was built; the Emperor moved to the Prince of Kuaiji's residence.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on yisi, construction began on the new palace and the Emperor moved into the Prince of Kuaiji's residence.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅遣征南大將軍、都督征討諸軍事、守尚書令長樂公丕、武衛將軍苟萇、尚書慕容□帥步騎七萬寇襄陽，以荊州刺史楊安帥樊、鄧之眾為前鋒，征虜將軍始平石越帥精騎一萬出魯陽關，京兆尹慕容垂、揚武將軍姚萇帥眾五萬出南鄉，領軍將軍苟池、右將軍毛當、強弩將軍王顯帥眾四萬出武當，會攻襄陽。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin sent Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, General Who Conquers the South, Commander-in-Chief of all Expeditionary Forces, and Keeper of the Masters of Writing; Gou Chang, Martial Guard General; and Murong Wei, Master of Writing, to lead seventy thousand infantry and cavalry to invade Xiangyang. Yang An, Inspector of Jingzhou, led the forces of Fan and Deng as vanguard; Shi Yue of Shiping, General Who Captures Barbarians, led ten thousand elite cavalry out through Luyang Pass; Murong Chui, Intendant of Jingzhao, and Yao Chang, General Who Displays Martial Prowess, led fifty thousand men out through Nanxiang; Gou Chi, Army Supervisor General; Mao Dang, Right General; and Wang Xian, Strong Crossbow General, led forty thousand men out through Wudang — all converging to attack Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian dispatched Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, General Who Conquers the South and overall commander; Gou Chang, Martial Guard General; and Murong Wei, Master of Writing, with seventy thousand infantry and cavalry against Xiangyang. Yang An, Inspector of Jingzhou, led the troops of Fan and Deng as vanguard. Shi Yue of Shiping, General Who Captures Barbarians, took ten thousand elite cavalry through Luyang Pass. Murong Chui, Intendant of Jingzhao, and Yao Chang, General Who Displays Martial Prowess, marched fifty thousand men through Nanxiang. Gou Chi, Army Supervisor; Mao Dang, Right General; and Wang Xian, Strong Crossbow General, brought forty thousand through Wudang. All converged on Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，秦兵至沔北，梁州刺史朱序以秦無舟楫，不以為虞。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Qin troops reached the north bank of the Mian; Zhu Xu, Inspector of Liangzhou, considering that Qin had no boats, did not regard it as a threat.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Qin forces reached the north bank of the Han. Zhu Xu, Inspector of Liangzhou, assumed they posed no threat without boats.

sentences.zh: 既而石越帥騎五千浮渡漢水，序惶駭，固守中城。

translations.literal: Before long Shi Yue led five thousand cavalry to cross the Han floating on rafts; Xu was alarmed and terrified, and held firm in the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: Then Shi Yue led five thousand cavalry across the Han on rafts. Zhu Xu was struck with terror and withdrew into the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 越克其外郭，獲船百餘艘以濟餘軍。

translations.literal: Yue took the outer wall, obtained more than a hundred boats, and used them to ferry the remaining army.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue captured the outer wall, seized more than a hundred boats, and used them to ferry the rest of the army across.

sentences.zh: 長樂公丕督諸將攻中城。

translations.literal: Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, directed the various generals in attacking the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, directed the generals in the assault on the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 序母韓氏聞秦兵將至，自登城履行，至西北隅，以為不固，帥百餘婢及城中女丁築邪城於其內。

translations.literal: Xu's mother, Lady Han, hearing that Qin troops were about to arrive, herself ascended the wall to inspect; reaching the northwest corner, she considered it unsound and led more than a hundred maidservants and women of the city to build an outer wall within.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xu's mother, Lady Han, learned that Qin troops were approaching, she walked the battlements herself. At the northwest corner she found the defenses weak and led more than a hundred maidservants and townswomen to build an inner parapet wall.

sentences.zh: 及秦兵至，西北隅果潰，眾移守新城，襄陽人謂之夫人城，桓沖在上明，擁眾七萬，憚秦兵之強，不敢進。

translations.literal: When Qin troops arrived, the northwest corner indeed collapsed; the multitude shifted to defend the new wall. The people of Xiangyang called it the Lady's Wall. Huan Chong was at Shangming with seventy thousand followers but feared Qin troops' strength and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin attacked, the northwest corner gave way as Lady Han had feared. The defenders fell back to her new wall — the people of Xiangyang called it the Lady's Wall. Huan Chong held Shangming with seventy thousand men but dared not advance against Qin's might.

sentences.zh: 丕欲急攻襄陽，苟萇曰：「吾眾十倍於敵，糗糧山積，但稍遷漢、沔之民於許、洛，塞其運道，絕其援兵，譬如網中之禽，何患不獲。

translations.literal: Pi wished to attack Xiangyang urgently; Gou Chang said: "Our multitude is ten times the enemy's; provisions are heaped like mountains. Only gradually relocate the people of Han and Mian to Xu and Luo, block their supply routes, and cut off their reinforcements — like birds in a net, what worry is there of not capturing them?
translations.idiomatic: Pi wanted a swift assault on Xiangyang, but Gou Chang urged patience: "We outnumber them ten to one and our supplies are piled like hills. Relocate the Han and Mian populace gradually to Xu and Luoyang, block their supply lines, and cut off reinforcements. They will be birds in a net — how can they escape?

sentences.zh: 而多殺將士，急求成功哉！」

translations.literal: Yet slaughter many officers and soldiers, urgently seeking quick success!"
translations.idiomatic: Why slaughter our own troops in a reckless rush for victory?"

sentences.zh: 丕從之。

translations.literal: Pi followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Pi agreed.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂拔南陽，執太守鄭裔，與丕會襄陽。

translations.literal: Murong Chui took Nanyang, seized Administrator Zheng Yi, and joined Pi at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui captured Nanyang, took its administrator Zheng Yi prisoner, and rendezvoused with Pi at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，新宮成；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the new palace was completed;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the new palace was finished;

sentences.zh: 辛巳，帝入居之。

translations.literal: On xinsi, the Emperor moved in to reside there.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the Emperor took up residence in it.

sentences.zh: 秦兗州刺史彭超請攻沛郡太守逯於彭城，且曰：「願更遣重將攻淮南諸城，為征南棋劫之勢，東西並進，丹楊不足平也。」

translations.literal: Peng Chao, Inspector of Yanzhou of Qin, requested to attack Lu, Administrator of Pei Commandery, at Pengcheng, and further said: "I wish additionally to send a weighty general to attack the various cities of Huainan, creating for the southern expedition the momentum of a chess abduction — advancing east and west together, Danyang would not be difficult to pacify."
translations.idiomatic: Peng Chao, Qin's Inspector of Yanzhou, asked to attack Lu, Administrator of Pei, at Pengcheng and added, "Send another senior commander against the Huainan cities to support the southern campaign with a pincer from east and west. Danyang would then fall easily."

sentences.zh: 秦王堅從之，使都督東討諸軍事；

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin followed this; he made Peng Chao Commander-in-Chief of all Eastern Expedition Forces;
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian agreed and appointed him Commander-in-Chief of the Eastern Expedition;

sentences.zh: 後將軍俱難、右禁將軍毛盛、洛州刺史邵保帥步騎七萬寇淮陽、盱眙。

translations.literal: Rear General Ju Nan, Right Guard General Mao Sheng, and Shao Bao, Inspector of Luozhou, led seventy thousand infantry and cavalry to raid Huaiyang and Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Rear General Ju Nan, Right Guard General Mao Sheng, and Shao Bao, Inspector of Luozhou, led seventy thousand infantry and cavalry against Huaiyang and Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 超，越之弟；

translations.literal: Chao was Yue's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Chao was Yue's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 保，羌之從弟也。

translations.literal: Bao was Qiang's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was Qiang's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 八月，彭超攻彭城，詔右將軍毛虎生帥眾五萬鎮姑孰以御秦兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Peng Chao attacked Pengcheng. An edict ordered Right General Mao Husheng to lead fifty thousand troops to garrison Gudu and resist Qin forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Peng Chao attacked Pengcheng. The court ordered Right General Mao Husheng to lead fifty thousand men to garrison Gudu and hold the Qin army at bay.

sentences.zh: 秦梁州刺史韋鐘圍魏興太守吉挹於西城。

translations.literal: Wei Zhong, Inspector of Liangzhou for Qin, besieged Ji Yi, Administrator of Weixing, at Xicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhong, Qin's Inspector of Liangzhou, besieged Ji Yi, Administrator of Weixing, at Xicheng.

sentences.zh: 九月，秦王堅與群臣飲酒，以秘書監朱肜為正，命人人以極醉為限。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, King Fu Jian drank wine with his ministers. He made Zhu Rong, Director of the Secretariat, the toastmaster and ordered each man to drink until utterly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, King Fu Jian feasted with his ministers, appointed Zhu Rong, Director of the Secretariat, as toastmaster, and ordered everyone to drink until completely drunk.

sentences.zh: 秘書侍郎趙整作《酒德之歌》曰：「地列酒泉，天垂酒池，杜康妙識，儀狄先知。

translations.literal: Secretariat Gentleman Zhao Zheng composed "Song of Wine Virtue," saying: "On earth the Spring of Wine is arrayed; in heaven the Wine Pool hangs down. Du Kang saw it with subtle insight; Yi Di knew it beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Gentleman Zhao Zheng composed the "Song of Wine Virtue," saying, "On earth stands the Spring of Wine; from heaven hangs the Wine Pool. Du Kang grasped its secret; Yi Di knew it first.

sentences.zh: 紂喪殷邦，桀傾夏國，由此言之，前危後則。」

translations.literal: Zhou lost the state of Yin; Jie toppled the state of Xia — speaking from this, peril comes before and follows after."
translations.idiomatic: Zhou lost the Yin dynasty; Jie brought down the Xia — from this we see danger ahead and ruin behind."

sentences.zh: 堅大悅，命整書之以為酒戒，自是宴群臣，禮飲而已。

translations.literal: Fu Jian was greatly pleased. He ordered Zheng to write it out as a warning against wine. From then on when he feasted ministers, he drank only ceremonially.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was delighted and had Zheng write it out as a warning against wine. After that, when he feasted his ministers, he drank only in moderation.

sentences.zh: 秦涼州刺史梁熙遣使入西域，揚秦威德。

translations.literal: Liang Xi, Inspector of Liangzhou for Qin, sent emissaries into the Western Regions to proclaim Qin's majesty and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi, Qin's Inspector of Liangzhou, sent envoys into the Western Regions to proclaim Qin's power and virtue.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，大宛獻汗血馬。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Dayuan presented sweat-blood horses.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Dayuan presented sweat-blood horses.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅曰：「吾嘗慕漢文帝之為人，用千里馬何為！

translations.literal: King Fu Jian said: "I have always admired the character of Emperor Wen of Han — what use have I for thousand-li horses!
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian said, "I have always admired Emperor Wen of Han — what need have I for thousand-li horses!

sentences.zh: 命群臣作《止馬之詩》而反之。

translations.literal: He ordered the ministers to compose "Poem on Stopping the Horse" and sent the horses back.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his ministers to compose the "Poem on Stopping the Horse" and returned the horses.

sentences.zh: 巴西人趙寶起兵梁州，自稱晉西蠻校尉、巴郡太守。

translations.literal: Zhao Bao of Baxi raised troops in Liangzhou, styling himself Jin Western Man Commander and Administrator of Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bao of Baxi raised an army in Liangzhou and styled himself Jin Western Man Commander and Administrator of Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 秦豫州刺史北海公重鎮洛陽，謀反。

translations.literal: Zhong, Duke of Beihai, commanded Luoyang as Inspector of Yuzhou for Qin and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong, Duke of Beihai, held Luoyang as Qin's Inspector of Yuzhou and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅曰：「長史呂光忠正，必不與之同。」

translations.literal: King Fu Jian said: "Chief Clerk Lü Guang is loyal and upright — he will surely not join him."
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian said, "Chief Clerk Lü Guang is loyal and upright — he will surely not join the plot."

sentences.zh: 即命光收重，檻車送長安，赦之，以公就第。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Guang to seize Zhong, send him to Chang'an in a caged cart, pardoned him, and let him live at home as a duke.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered Lü Guang to arrest Zhong, send him to Chang'an in a caged cart, pardoned him, and allowed him to live at home as a duke.

sentences.zh: 重，洛之兄也。

translations.literal: Zhong was Luo's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was Luo's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 十二月，秦御史中丞李柔劾秦：「長樂公丕等擁眾十萬，攻圍小城，日費萬金，久而無效，請微下廷尉。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Li Rou, Censor-in-Chief of Qin, impeached Qin, saying: "Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, and others command one hundred thousand men, besiege a small city, spend ten thousand in gold per day, and after long effort achieve nothing. I request they be lightly sent down to the Minister of Justice."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Li Rou, Qin's Censor-in-Chief, impeached the court, saying, "Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, and his command of one hundred thousand men have besieged a small city, spending ten thousand in gold each day, yet after long months have achieved nothing. I ask that they be referred to the Minister of Justice."

sentences.zh: 秦王堅曰：「丕等廣費無成，實宜貶戮；

translations.literal: King Fu Jian said: "Pi and the others have spent lavishly without result — they truly deserve demotion and punishment;
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian said, "Pi and the others have squandered resources without success — they truly deserve demotion and punishment;

sentences.zh: 但師已淹時，不可虛返，其特原之，令以成功贖罪。」

translations.literal: but the army has already been long delayed and cannot return empty-handed. Let them be specially pardoned and commanded to redeem their guilt through success."
translations.idiomatic: but the campaign has dragged on too long to withdraw empty-handed. Let them be specially pardoned and ordered to redeem their guilt through victory."

sentences.zh: 使黃門侍郎韋華持節切讓丕等，賜丕劍曰：「來春不捷，汝可自裁，勿復持面見吾也！」

translations.literal: He sent Palace Attendant Wei Hua with credentials to sternly rebuke Pi and the others, and granted Pi a sword, saying: "If you do not prevail next spring, you may kill yourselves — do not again come before me holding your faces!"
