translations.idiomatic: He sent Palace Attendant Wei Hua with credentials to sternly rebuke Pi and the others, and gave Pi a sword, saying, "If you have not won by next spring, kill yourselves — do not come before me again!"

sentences.zh: 周颺在秦，密與桓沖書，言秦陰計；

translations.literal: Zhou Yang was in Qin and secretly wrote to Huan Chong about Qin's secret plans;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yang was in Qin and secretly wrote to Huan Chong revealing Qin's secret plans;

sentences.zh: 又逃奔漢中，秦人獲而赦之。

translations.literal: he also fled to Hanzhong, was captured by Qin men, and pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: he then fled to Hanzhong, was captured by Qin forces, and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝上之中太元四年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — fourth year of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — fourth year of Taiyuan (

sentences.zh: 己卯，公元三七九年）

translations.literal: jimao, corresponding to 379 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jimao year, 379 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛酉，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinyou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinyou, the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 秦長樂公丕等得詔惶恐，乃命諸軍並力攻襄陽。

translations.literal: Fu Pi, Duke of Changle of Qin, and the others, receiving the edict in fear, then ordered all armies to join forces and attack Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, and the other Qin commanders, terrified by the edict, ordered all their armies to combine and assault Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅欲自將攻襄陽，詔陽平公融以關東六州之兵會壽春，梁熙以河西之兵為後繼。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian wished to lead the attack on Xiangyang in person. An edict ordered Fu Rong, Duke of Yangping, to assemble the armies of the six eastern provinces at Shouchun, with Liang Xi leading the Hexi forces as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian intended to lead the assault on Xiangyang himself. He ordered Fu Rong, Duke of Yangping, to gather the armies of the six eastern provinces at Shouchun, with Liang Xi's Hexi forces as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 陽平公融諫曰：「陛下欲取江南，固當博謀熟慮，不可倉猝。

translations.literal: Fu Rong, Duke of Yangping, remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty wishes to take the lands south of the Yangtze — you should certainly deliberate broadly and consider carefully; you must not act in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong, Duke of Yangping, remonstrated, saying, "If Your Majesty means to conquer the south, you should plan carefully and not act in haste.

sentences.zh: 若止取襄陽，又豈足親勞大駕乎？

translations.literal: If you are only taking Xiangyang, is it worth troubling the imperial presence in person?
translations.idiomatic: If you are only taking Xiangyang, is it worth the Son of Heaven going in person?

sentences.zh: 未有動天下之眾而為一城者，所謂以隨侯之珠彈千仞之雀也。」

translations.literal: Never before has one moved the armies of the empire for a single city — this is what they call using the Sui Marquis's pearl to shoot a sparrow a thousand fathoms up."
translations.idiomatic: Never before has the empire's full force been mobilized for one city — it is like using the Marquis of Sui's pearl to shoot a sparrow a thousand fathoms above."

sentences.zh: 梁熙諫曰：「晉主之暴，未如孫皓，江山險固，易守難攻。

translations.literal: Liang Xi remonstrated, saying: "The Jin ruler's cruelty does not match that of Sun Hao; the rivers and mountains are steep and firm, easy to defend and hard to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi remonstrated, saying, "The Jin emperor is not as cruel as Sun Hao was, and the rivers and mountains are steep and strong — easy to hold and hard to take.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲廓清江表，亦不過分命將帥，引關東之兵，南臨淮、泗，下梁、益之卒，東出巴、峽，又何必親屈鸞輅，遠幸沮澤乎？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty must clear the lands south of the Yangtze, it is enough simply to assign generals, bring the armies of the east down to the Huai and Si, send the troops of Liang and Yi southward, and march the forces of Ba and the Gorges eastward — why must you personally bend the imperial carriage and travel far to marshlands?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly means to pacify the south, you need only dispatch generals — bring eastern armies to the Huai and Si, send Liang and Yi troops south, and march Ba and Gorge forces east. Why must the imperial carriage travel far into marshlands?

sentences.zh: 昔漢光武誅公孫述，晉武帝擒孫皓，未聞二帝自統六師，親執枹鼓，蒙矢石也。」

translations.literal: In former times Emperor Guangwu of Han destroyed Gongsun Shu, and Emperor Wu of Jin captured Sun Hao — one never heard of either emperor personally commanding the six armies, holding drumsticks, and exposing himself to arrows and stones."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu of Han destroyed Gongsun Shu and Emperor Wu of Jin captured Sun Hao, neither emperor personally led the six armies, beat the war drums, or faced arrows and stones."

sentences.zh: 堅乃止。

translations.literal: Fu Jian then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 詔冠軍將軍南郡相劉波帥眾八千救襄陽，波畏秦，不敢進。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Liu Bo, Champion General and Administrator of Nanjun, to lead eight thousand men to rescue Xiangyang. Bo feared Qin and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Liu Bo, Champion General and Administrator of Nanjun, to lead eight thousand men to relieve Xiangyang, but Bo feared Qin and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 朱序屢出戰，破秦兵，引退稍遠，序不設備。

translations.literal: Zhu Xu repeatedly sallied forth to fight, defeated Qin troops, and as they withdrew somewhat farther, Xu made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu repeatedly sallied out and defeated Qin forces. As the enemy withdrew farther away, Xu lowered his guard.

sentences.zh: 二月，襄陽督護李伯護密遣其子送款於秦，請為內應；

translations.literal: In the second month, Li Bohu, Supervisor of Xiangyang, secretly sent his son to submit to Qin and request to serve as an inside collaborator;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Li Bohu, Supervisor of Xiangyang, secretly sent his son to Qin to offer surrender and ask to serve as an inside collaborator;

sentences.zh: 長樂公丕命諸軍進攻之。

translations.literal: Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, ordered all armies to press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi, Duke of Changle, ordered all armies to press the assault.

sentences.zh: 戊午，克襄陽，執朱序，送長安。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Xiangyang was taken. Zhu Xu was captured and sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Xiangyang fell. Zhu Xu was captured and sent to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅以序能守節，拜度支尚書；

translations.literal: King Fu Jian, considering that Xu had upheld his integrity, appointed him Minister of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian, impressed that Xu had held firm, appointed him Minister of Revenue;

sentences.zh: 以李伯護為不忠，斬之。

translations.literal: Li Bohu he deemed disloyal and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bohu he judged disloyal and had executed.

sentences.zh: 秦將軍慕容越拔順陽，執太守譙國丁穆。

translations.literal: Murong Yue, General of Qin, took Shunyang and captured Ding Mu of Qiaoguo, the Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yue, a Qin general, captured Shunyang and seized Ding Mu of Qiaoguo, the Administrator.

sentences.zh: 堅欲官之，穆固辭不受。

translations.literal: Fu Jian wished to give him office, but Mu firmly refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian wished to appoint him to office, but Mu steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 堅以中壘將軍梁成為荊州刺史，配兵一萬，鎮襄陽，選其才望，禮而用之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian made Liang Cheng, Middle Rampart General, Inspector of Jingzhou, assigned him ten thousand troops to garrison Xiangyang, and selected men of talent and reputation to honor and employ.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian appointed Liang Cheng, Middle Rampart General, as Inspector of Jingzhou, gave him ten thousand troops to garrison Xiangyang, and selected men of talent and standing to honor and employ.

sentences.zh: 桓沖以襄陽陷沒，上疏送章節，請解職；

translations.literal: Huan Chong, because Xiangyang had fallen, submitted a memorial returning his seal and cord and requesting to resign;
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangyang fell, Huan Chong submitted a memorial returning his seal and cord and asking to resign;

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.

sentences.zh: 詔免劉波官，俄復以為冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: An edict removed Liu Bo from office, but soon afterward restored him as Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: The court stripped Liu Bo of his post, but soon restored him as Champion General.

sentences.zh: 秦以前將軍張蚝為并州刺史。

translations.literal: Qin made Zhang Hao, former General, Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin appointed Zhang Hao, former General, as Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史謝玄帥眾萬餘救彭城，軍於泗口，欲遣間使報戴逯而不可得。

translations.literal: Xie Xuan, Inspector of Yanzhou, led more than ten thousand men to rescue Pengcheng and encamped at Sikou. He wished to send a secret messenger to inform Dai Lu but could not manage it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan, Inspector of Yanzhou, led more than ten thousand men to relieve Pengcheng and encamped at Sikou. He wanted to send a secret messenger to warn Dai Lu but could find no way.

sentences.zh: 部曲將田泓請沒水潛行趣彭城，玄遣之。

translations.literal: Tian Hong, a subordinate commander, asked to dive underwater and slip through to Pengcheng; Xuan sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hong, a subordinate commander, volunteered to swim underwater to reach Pengcheng, and Xuan sent him.

sentences.zh: 泓為秦人所獲，厚賂之，使雲南軍已敗；

translations.literal: Hong was captured by Qin men, who bribed him heavily and made him say the southern army had already been defeated;
translations.idiomatic: Hong was captured by Qin troops, who bribed him heavily and ordered him to claim the southern army had already been defeated;

sentences.zh: 泓偽許之，既而告城中曰：「南軍垂至，我單行來報，為賊所得。

translations.literal: Hong falsely agreed, then told the city: "The southern army is about to arrive — I came alone to report and was seized by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Hong pretended to agree, then shouted to the city, "The southern army is almost here! I came alone to bring word and was captured by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 勉之！」

translations.literal: Take heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Hold firm!"

sentences.zh: 秦人殺之。

translations.literal: The Qin men killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin troops killed him.

sentences.zh: 彭超置輜重於留城，謝玄揚聲遣後軍將軍東海何謙向留城。

translations.literal: Peng Chao placed his baggage train at Liucheng. Xie Xuan loudly announced he was sending Rear Army General He Qian of Donghai toward Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Chao had left his baggage train at Liucheng. Xie Xuan publicly announced he was sending Rear Army General He Qian of Donghai toward Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 超聞之，釋彭城圍，引兵還保輜重。

translations.literal: When Chao heard this, he lifted the siege of Pengcheng, withdrew his troops, and returned to protect the baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao heard this, he broke off the siege of Pengcheng and marched back to protect his baggage train.

sentences.zh: 戴逯帥彭城之眾，隨謙奔玄，超遂據彭城，留兗州治中徐褒守之，南攻盱眙。

translations.literal: Dai Lu led the people of Pengcheng, followed Qian, and fled to Xuan. Chao then occupied Pengcheng, left Xu Bao, Administrator-in-Chief of Yanzhou, to hold it, and marched south to attack Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Lu led the people of Pengcheng, followed He Qian, and joined Xie Xuan. Chao then seized Pengcheng, left Xu Bao, Administrator-in-Chief of Yanzhou, to defend it, and marched south against Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 俱難克淮陰，留邵保戍之。

translations.literal: Ju Nan took Huaiyin and left Shao Bao to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Nan captured Huaiyin and left Shao Bao to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬戌，詔以「疆埸多虞，年穀不登，其供御所須，事從儉約；

translations.literal: In the third month, on renxu, an edict declared: "The frontier has many alarms and the year's grain has not ripened. What is required for the imperial household should be kept frugal;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renxu, an edict declared, "The frontiers are troubled and the harvest has failed. Imperial expenses must be kept frugal;

sentences.zh: 九親供給，眾官廩俸，權可減半。

translations.literal: the stipends of the nine kin and the grain salaries of all officials may provisionally be cut in half.
translations.idiomatic: stipends for the nine degrees of kin and salaries for all officials may be cut in half for now.

sentences.zh: 凡諸役費，自非軍國事要，皆宜停省。」

translations.literal: Of all labor and expenses, whatever is not essential to military and state affairs should be halted and reduced."
translations.idiomatic: All other levies and expenditures not essential to military or state affairs should be suspended."

sentences.zh: 癸未，使右將軍毛虎生帥眾三萬擊巴中，以救魏興。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Right General Mao Husheng was sent to lead thirty thousand men to attack Bazhong and relieve Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Right General Mao Husheng was sent with thirty thousand men to attack Bazhong and relieve Weixing.

sentences.zh: 前鋒督護趙福等至巴西，為秦將張紹等所敗，亡七千餘人。

translations.literal: Zhao Fu and other vanguard supervisors reached Baxi and were defeated by Qin generals Zhang Shao and others, losing more than seven thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard supervisors Zhao Fu and others reached Baxi and were defeated by Qin generals Zhang Shao and others, losing more than seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 虎生退屯巴東。

translations.literal: Husheng withdrew and encamped at Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Husheng withdrew and encamped at Badong.

sentences.zh: 蜀人李烏聚眾二萬，圍成都以應虎生，秦王堅使破虜將軍呂光擊滅之。

translations.literal: Li Wu of Shu gathered twenty thousand men, besieged Chengdu in support of Husheng. King Fu Jian sent Lü Guang, General Who Breaks Barbarians, to attack and destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wu of Shu gathered twenty thousand men and besieged Chengdu in support of Husheng. King Fu Jian sent Lü Guang, General Who Breaks Barbarians, to crush him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊申，韋鐘拔魏興，吉挹引刀欲自殺，左右奪其刀；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wushen, Wei Zhong took Weixing. Ji Yi drew a knife intending suicide, but attendants seized the blade;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on wushen, Wei Zhong captured Weixing. Ji Yi drew a knife to kill himself, but attendants wrested it away;

sentences.zh: 會秦人至，執之，挹不言不食而死。

translations.literal: just then Qin men arrived, seized him, and Yi, speaking not and eating not, died.
translations.idiomatic: then Qin troops arrived and seized him. Yi refused to speak or eat, and died.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅歎曰：「周孟威不屈於前，丁彥遠潔己於後，吉祖沖閉口而死，何晉氏之多忠臣也！」

translations.literal: King Fu Jian sighed and said: "Zhou Mengwei would not yield before; Ding Yanyuan kept himself pure after; Ji Zuchong closed his mouth and died — how many loyal ministers the Jin house has!"
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian sighed and said, "Zhou Mengwei would not submit; Ding Yanyuan kept himself pure; Ji Zuchong sealed his lips and died — how many loyal ministers the Jin have!"

sentences.zh: 挹參軍史穎逃歸，得挹臨終手疏，詔贈益州刺史。

translations.literal: Yi's staff officer Shi Ying escaped back, obtained Yi's final handwritten memorial, and an edict posthumously made him Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's staff officer Shi Ying escaped home with Ji's final handwritten memorial, and the court posthumously appointed him Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 秦毛當、王顯帥眾二萬自襄陽東會俱難、彭超攻淮南。

translations.literal: Mao Dang and Wang Xian of Qin led twenty thousand men east from Xiangyang to join Ju Nan and Peng Chao in attacking Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dang and Wang Xian of Qin led twenty thousand men east from Xiangyang to join Ju Nan and Peng Chao in the Huainan campaign.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙丑，難、超拔盱眙，執高密內史毛璪之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yichou, Nan and Chao took Xuyi and captured Mao Zanzhi, Interior Minister of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yichou, Ju Nan and Peng Chao captured Xuyi and seized Mao Zanzhi, Interior Minister of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 秦兵六萬圍幽州刺史田洛於三阿，去廣陵百里；

translations.literal: Sixty thousand Qin troops besieged Tian Luo, Inspector of Youzhou, at San'a, one hundred li from Guangling;
translations.idiomatic: Sixty thousand Qin troops besieged Tian Luo, Inspector of Youzhou, at San'a, a hundred li from Guangling;

sentences.zh: 朝廷大震，臨江列戍，遣征虜將軍謝石帥舟師屯塗中。

translations.literal: the court was greatly shaken, lined garrisons along the Yangtze, and sent Xie Shi, General Who Captures Barbarians, to lead the fleet and encamp at Tuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: the court was shaken, lined the Yangtze with garrisons, and sent Xie Shi, General Who Captures Barbarians, to lead the fleet and encamp at Tuzhong.

sentences.zh: 石，安之弟也。

translations.literal: Shi was An's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was Xie An's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 右衛將軍毛安之等帥眾四萬屯堂邑。

translations.literal: Mao Anzhi and others, Right Guard Generals, led forty thousand men to encamp at Tangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Anzhi, Right Guard General, and others led forty thousand men to encamp at Tangyi.

sentences.zh: 秦毛當、毛盛帥騎二萬襲堂邑，安之等驚潰。

translations.literal: Mao Dang and Mao Sheng of Qin led twenty thousand cavalry to raid Tangyi; Anzhi and the others panicked and fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dang and Mao Sheng of Qin led twenty thousand cavalry in a surprise attack on Tangyi; Anzhi and his men panicked and fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史謝玄自廣陵救三阿；

translations.literal: Xie Xuan, Inspector of Yanzhou, came from Guangling to rescue San'a;
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan, Inspector of Yanzhou, marched from Guangling to relieve San'a;

sentences.zh: 丙子，難、超戰敗，退保盱眙。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Nan and Chao were defeated in battle and withdrew to hold Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Ju Nan and Peng Chao were defeated and withdrew to Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊子，玄與田洛帥眾五萬進攻盱眙，難、超又敗，退屯淮陰。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuzi, Xuan and Tian Luo led fifty thousand men to attack Xuyi. Nan and Chao were defeated again and withdrew to encamp at Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuzi, Xie Xuan and Tian Luo led fifty thousand men against Xuyi. Ju Nan and Peng Chao were beaten again and fell back to Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 玄遣何謙等帥舟師乘潮而上，夜，焚淮橋。

translations.literal: Xuan sent He Qian and others to lead the fleet upstream on the tide; at night they burned the Huai bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent He Qian and others with the fleet to ride the tide upstream; by night they burned the bridge over the Huai.

sentences.zh: 邵保戰死，難，超退屯淮北，玄與何謙、戴逯、田洛共追之，戰於君川，復大破之，難、超北走，僅以身免。

translations.literal: Shao Bao died in battle. Nan and Chao withdrew to encamp north of the Huai. Xuan, together with He Qian, Dai Lu, and Tian Luo, pursued them, fought at Junchuan, and again routed them heavily. Nan and Chao fled north and barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Bao was killed in battle. Ju Nan and Peng Chao withdrew north of the Huai. Xuan, He Qian, Dai Lu, and Tian Luo pursued them, fought at Junchuan, and routed them again. Nan and Chao fled north and barely escaped with their lives.

sentences.zh: 謝玄還廣陵，詔進號冠軍將軍，加領徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Xie Xuan returned to Guangling. An edict advanced his title to Champion General and additionally made him Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan returned to Guangling. The court promoted him to Champion General and additionally appointed him Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅聞之，大怒。

translations.literal: When King Fu Jian heard of it, he was furious.
translations.idiomatic: When King Fu Jian heard the news, he was furious.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，檻車徵超下廷尉，超自殺。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Chao was summoned to the Minister of Justice in a caged cart; Chao killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Peng Chao was summoned to the Minister of Justice in a caged cart and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 難削爵為民。

translations.literal: Nan was stripped of rank and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Nan was stripped of his noble rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 以毛當為徐州刺吏，鎮彭城；

translations.literal: Mao Dang was made Inspector of Xuzhou and garrisoned Pengcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dang was appointed Inspector of Xuzhou and garrisoned Pengcheng;

sentences.zh: 毛盛為兗州刺史，鎮胡陸；

translations.literal: Mao Sheng was made Inspector of Yanzhou and garrisoned Hulu;
translations.idiomatic: Mao Sheng was appointed Inspector of Yanzhou and garrisoned Hulu;

sentences.zh: 王顯為揚州刺史，戍下邳。

translations.literal: Wang Xian was made Inspector of Yangzhou and garrisoned Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian was appointed Inspector of Yangzhou and garrisoned Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 謝安為宰相，秦人屢入寇，邊兵失利，眾心危懼，安每鎮之，以和靜。

translations.literal: Xie An was chief minister. Qin men repeatedly invaded, frontier troops suffered defeats, and popular sentiment was fearful — An each time calmed it with harmony and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An served as chief minister. Qin forces repeatedly raided the borders, frontier troops suffered defeats, and the people grew fearful — yet An always steadied them with calm and composure.

sentences.zh: 其為政，務舉大綱，不為小察。

translations.literal: In his governance he strove to grasp the great outline and did not fuss over small scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: In governing, he focused on the broad principles and did not fuss over petty details.

sentences.zh: 時人比安於王導，而謂其文雅過之。

translations.literal: People of the time compared An to Wang Dao, but said his refinement surpassed Dao's.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries compared him to Wang Dao, but judged his refinement superior.

sentences.zh: 八月，丁亥，以左將軍王蘊為尚書僕射，頃之，遷丹楊尹。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on dinghai, Wang Yun was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; before long he was transferred to Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dinghai, Wang Yun was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; soon afterward he was transferred to Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 蘊自以國姻，不欲在內，苦求外出；

translations.literal: Yun, considering himself connected to the imperial house by marriage, did not wish to serve within the capital and bitterly sought an outside post;
translations.idiomatic: Yun, as a relative by marriage to the imperial house, did not wish to serve at court and urgently sought a post outside the capital;

sentences.zh: 復以為都督浙江東五郡諸軍事、會稽內史。

translations.literal: he was again made Commander of all Military Affairs in the Five Commanderies East of the Zhe River and Interior Minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: he was again made Commander of all Military Affairs in the Five Commanderies East of the Zhe River and Interior Minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 是歲，秦大饑。

translations.literal: This year Qin suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qin suffered a severe famine.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝上之中太元五年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — fifth year of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — fifth year of Taiyuan (

sentences.zh: 庚辰，公元三八零年）

translations.literal: gengchen, corresponding to 380 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengchen year, 380 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，秦王堅復以北海公重為鎮北大將軍，鎮薊。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, King Fu Jian of Qin again appointed Duke Zhong of Beihai as Great General Who Guards the North and garrisoned Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, King Fu Jian of Qin again appointed Duke Zhong of Beihai Great General Who Guards the North, with his command at Ji.

sentences.zh: 二月，作教武堂於渭城，命太學生明陰陽兵法者教授諸將。

translations.literal: In the second month, they built the Hall for Teaching Warfare at Weicheng and ordered Imperial University students who understood yin-yang and military tactics to instruct the generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the Hall for Teaching Warfare was built at Weicheng, and Imperial University students versed in yin-yang doctrine and military strategy were ordered to instruct the generals.

sentences.zh: 秘書監朱肜諫曰：「陛下東征西伐，所向無敵，四海之地，什得其八，雖江南未服，蓋不足言，是宜稍偃武事，增修文德。

translations.literal: Privy Treasurer Zhu Rong remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty campaigns east and west — wherever you go, none can stand; of all the land within the four seas, you hold eight parts in ten. Though the lands south of the Yangtze are not yet subdued, that is scarcely worth mentioning. You ought now to ease off military affairs somewhat and further cultivate civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Treasurer Zhu Rong remonstrated: "Your Majesty has campaigned east and west without meeting a foe who could stand against you; you hold eight-tenths of the land within the four seas. Though the south of the Yangtze is not yet subdued, that hardly matters — it is time to ease off warfare and cultivate civil virtue.

sentences.zh: 乃更始立學舍，教人戰鬥之術，殆非所以馴致昇平也。

translations.literal: Yet now you newly establish schoolhouses to teach men the arts of fighting — this is scarcely the way to gently bring about a time of lasting peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now you are establishing schools to teach the arts of combat — this is hardly the way to bring about lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 且諸將皆百戰之餘，何患不習於兵，而更使受教於書生，非所以強其志氣也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the generals are all veterans of a hundred battles — what worry is there that they are not practiced in war? Yet you would have them receive instruction from bookish scholars — this does not strengthen their fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, your generals are all veterans of a hundred battles — there is no need to worry that they lack military skill. To have them receive instruction from bookish scholars does nothing to strengthen their fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 此無益於實而有損於名，惟陛下圖之！」

translations.literal: This benefits nothing in substance yet damages your reputation. Your Majesty, please consider this!"
translations.idiomatic: This gains nothing in substance yet damages your reputation. Your Majesty, please consider it!"

sentences.zh: 堅乃止。

translations.literal: Fu Jian then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 秦征北將軍、幽州刺史行唐公洛，勇而多力，能坐制奔牛，射洞犁耳；

translations.literal: Qin's Northern Expeditionary General, Inspector of Youzhou, Duke Luo of Xingtang, was brave and very strong — he could while sitting subdue a charging ox and with an arrow pierce a plough handle;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Luo of Xingtang, Qin's Northern Expeditionary General and Inspector of Youzhou, was a man of great courage and strength — he could subdue a charging ox while seated and pierce a plough handle with an arrow;

sentences.zh: 自以有滅代之功，求開府儀同三司，不得，由是怨憤。

translations.literal: considering himself to have the merit of destroying Dai, he sought the rank of Grand General with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies but did not obtain it — from this he nursed resentment and anger.
translations.idiomatic: believing himself entitled to credit for destroying Dai, he sought the rank of Grand General with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies but was refused, and from then on nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 三月，秦王堅以洛為使持節、都督益、寧、西南夷諸軍事、征南大將軍、益州牧，使自伊闕趨襄陽，溯漢而上。

translations.literal: In the third month, King Fu Jian of Qin made Luo Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of all Military Affairs in Yi, Ning, and the Southwestern Yi, Great General on Southern Expedition, and Governor of Yizhou, ordering him to set out from Yique, hurry to Xiangyang, and ascend the Han River upstream.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, King Fu Jian appointed Luo Bearer of the Staff of Authority, supreme commander of military affairs in Yi, Ning, and the southwestern Yi territories, Great General on Southern Expedition, and Governor of Yizhou, ordering him to set out from Yique for Xiangyang and ascend the Han River.

sentences.zh: 洛謂官屬曰：「孤，帝室至親，不得入為將相，而常擯棄邊鄙。

translations.literal: Luo said to his staff: "I, an emperor's kinsman of the closest degree, am not permitted to enter the capital as general or minister but am constantly cast off to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Luo said to his staff, "I am the emperor's closest kinsman, yet I am never allowed to serve in the capital as general or minister — I am always cast off to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 今又投之西裔，復不聽過京師，此必有陰計，欲使梁成沉孤於漢水耳。

translations.literal: Now I am again cast into the western regions and not even allowed to pass through the capital — there must be some hidden design here, intending to have Liang Cheng sink me in the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: Now I am being sent to the western marches and not even permitted to pass through the capital — this must be a hidden plot to have Liang Cheng destroy me on the Han.

sentences.zh: 於諸君意何如？」

translations.literal: What do you gentlemen think?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 幽州治中平規曰：「逆取順守，湯、武是也；

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of Youzhou Ping Gui said: "Taking the realm by force yet ruling it in accordance with Heaven — that was Tang and Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Ping Gui, chief clerk of Youzhou, said, "Tang and Wu seized the realm by force yet ruled in accordance with Heaven;

sentences.zh: 因禍為福，桓、文是也。

translations.literal: turning calamity into good fortune — that was Huan and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Jin turned calamity into good fortune.

sentences.zh: 主上雖不為昏暴，然窮兵黷武，民思有所息肩者，十室而九。

translations.literal: The sovereign, though not a tyrant, exhausts the state in constant warfare — in nine households out of ten the people long for a chance to rest their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign is no tyrant, yet his endless warfare has exhausted the people — nine households in ten long for relief.

sentences.zh: 若明公神旗一建，必率土雲從。

translations.literal: If my lord raises his sacred banner, all within the realm will surely rise like clouds to follow.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Lordship raise your banner, the whole land will rally to you like clouds gathering.

sentences.zh: 今跨據全燕，地盡東海，北總烏桓、鮮卑，東引句麗、百濟，控弦之士不減五十餘萬，奈何束手就徵，蹈不測之禍乎！」

translations.literal: Now you hold all of Yan, your territory reaching to the Eastern Sea; to the north you can muster the Wuhuan and Xianbei; to the east you can draw in Goguryeo and Baekje — archers under arms number no less than five hundred thousand. Why submit meekly to summons and walk into unforeseen disaster!"
translations.idiomatic: You hold all of Yan, your lands reaching to the Eastern Sea; in the north you command the Wuhuan and Xianbei, in the east you can draw on Goguryeo and Baekje — your armed force numbers at least five hundred thousand. Why submit meekly to a summons and walk into disaster?"

sentences.zh: 洛攘袂大言曰：「孤計決矣，沮謀者斬！」

translations.literal: Luo pushed up his sleeves and proclaimed loudly: "My decision is made — whoever obstructs this plan shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Luo pushed up his sleeves and declared, "My mind is made up — whoever dissents will be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 於是自稱大將軍、大都督、秦王。

translations.literal: Thereupon he styled himself Great General, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he styled himself Great General, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 以平規為幽州刺史，玄菟太守吉貞為左長史，遼東太守趙贊為左司馬，昌黎太守王蘊為右司馬，遼西太守王琳、北平太守皇甫傑、牧官都尉魏敷等為從事中郎。

translations.literal: He made Ping Gui Inspector of Youzhou, Administrator of Xuantu Ji Zhen Left Chief Clerk, Administrator of Liaodong Zhao Zan Left Chief Military Aide, Administrator of Changli Wang Yun Right Chief Military Aide, and Administrator of Liaoxi Wang Lin, Administrator of Beiping Huangfu Jie, Chief Herds Officer Wei Fu, and others Attending Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Ping Gui Inspector of Youzhou, Ji Zhen of Xuantu as Left Chief Clerk, Zhao Zan of Liaodong as Left Chief Military Aide, Wang Yun of Changli as Right Chief Military Aide, and Wang Lin of Liaoxi, Huangfu Jie of Beiping, and Wei Fu, Chief Herds Officer, as Attending Clerks.

sentences.zh: 分遣使者徵兵於鮮卑、烏桓、高句麗、百濟、新羅、休忍諸國，遣兵三萬助北海公重戍薊。

translations.literal: He dispatched envoys separately to levy troops from Xianbei, Wuhuan, Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla, Xiuren, and other states, and sent thirty thousand troops to help Duke Zhong of Beihai garrison Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched envoys to levy troops from the Xianbei, Wuhuan, Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla, and Xiuren peoples, and sent thirty thousand men to help Duke Zhong of Beihai hold Ji.

sentences.zh: 諸國皆曰：「吾為天子守籓，不能從行唐公為逆。」

translations.literal: All the states said: "We guard the frontier for the Son of Heaven — we cannot follow Duke Luo of Xingtang in rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: They all replied, "We guard the frontier for the Son of Heaven — we cannot follow Duke Luo of Xingtang in rebellion."

sentences.zh: 洛懼，欲止，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Luo grew afraid and wished to stop, but hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Luo grew alarmed and wanted to abandon the plan, but hesitated, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 王縵、王琳、皇甫傑、魏敷知其無成，欲告之；

translations.literal: Wang Man, Wang Lin, Huangfu Jie, and Wei Fu, knowing he would not succeed, wished to inform on him;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Man, Wang Lin, Huangfu Jie, and Wei Fu, seeing that the plot would fail, intended to inform against him;

sentences.zh: 洛皆殺之。

translations.literal: Luo had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Luo had them all put to death.

sentences.zh: 吉貞、趙贊曰：「今諸國不從，事乖本圖。

translations.literal: Ji Zhen and Zhao Zan said: "Now the various states will not follow — the affair has deviated from the original plan.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhen and Zhao Zan said, "The states refuse to follow — the plan has gone awry.

sentences.zh: 明公若憚益州之行者，當遣使奉表乞留，主上亦不慮不從。」

translations.literal: If my lord fears the journey to Yizhou, you should send an envoy presenting a memorial begging to remain — the sovereign will surely not refuse."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Lordship dreads the posting to Yizhou, send an envoy with a memorial begging to be allowed to stay — the emperor will surely grant it."

sentences.zh: 平規曰：「今事形頗露，何可中止！

translations.literal: Ping Gui said: "The affair is already quite exposed — how can it be halted!
translations.idiomatic: Ping Gui said, "Matters are already too far gone — there is no turning back!

sentences.zh: 宜聲言受詔，盡幽州之兵，南出常山，陽平公必郊迎；

translations.literal: You should announce that you have received an imperial order, muster all the forces of Youzhou, march south through Changshan — Duke Rong the Duke of Yangping will surely come out to the suburbs to welcome you;
translations.idiomatic: Announce that you have received imperial orders, muster all Youzhou's forces, and march south through Changshan — the Duke of Yangping will surely come out to welcome you;

sentences.zh: 因而執之，進據冀州，總關東之眾以圖西土，天下可指麾而定也。」

translations.literal: seize him in the process, advance to hold Jizhou, gather all the forces east of the passes to plan against the western lands — the realm can be settled at a wave of the hand."
translations.idiomatic: seize him when he does, advance to occupy Jizhou, and rally all the forces east of the passes to strike west — the realm can be won at a command."

sentences.zh: 洛從之。

translations.literal: Luo followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Luo agreed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，洛帥眾七萬發和龍。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Luo led seventy thousand men and set out from Helong.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Luo led seventy thousand men out of Helong.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅召群臣謀之，步兵校尉呂光曰：「行唐公以至親為逆，此天下所共疾。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin summoned his ministers to deliberate. Colonel of Foot Soldiers Lü Guang said: "Duke Luo of Xingtang, a man of the closest imperial kinship, has turned traitor — this is what all under Heaven together abhors.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian summoned his ministers for counsel. Lü Guang, Colonel of Foot Soldiers, said, "Duke Luo of Xingtang has rebelled despite his close kinship to the throne — all under Heaven alike despises this.

sentences.zh: 願假臣步騎五萬，取之如拾遺耳。」

translations.literal: I beg to be lent fifty thousand infantry and cavalry — I shall take him as easily as picking up something dropped on the road."
translations.idiomatic: Lend me fifty thousand infantry and cavalry, and I shall capture him as easily as picking up something dropped on the road."

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「重、洛兄弟，據東北一隅，兵賦全資，未可輕也。」

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "The brothers Zhong and Luo hold a corner of the northeast — their military levies and resources are fully intact; they cannot be taken lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "The brothers Zhong and Luo hold the northeast with full military strength — they must not be underestimated."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「彼眾迫於凶威，一時蟻聚耳。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Their crowd is forced together by fierce intimidation — for the moment they swarm like ants, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang replied, "Their followers are driven together by terror — they are only a swarm of ants for the moment.

sentences.zh: 若以大軍臨之，勢必瓦解，不足憂也。」

translations.literal: If a great army presses upon them, they will surely disintegrate — there is nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: When a great army appears, they will collapse — there is nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 堅乃遺使讓洛，使還和龍，當以幽州永為世封。

translations.literal: Fu Jian then sent an envoy to rebuke Luo, ordering him to return to Helong — Youzhou would be his hereditary fief forever.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent an envoy to rebuke Luo and ordered him to return to Helong, promising that Youzhou would be his hereditary fief forever.

sentences.zh: 洛謂使者曰：「汝還白東海王，幽州褊狹，不足以容萬乘，須王秦中以承高祖之業。

translations.literal: Luo said to the envoy: "Go back and tell the Prince of Donghai: Youzhou is cramped and narrow — it cannot hold an emperor's chariot. He must reign in Guanzhong to carry on the ancestral enterprise of the Founding Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Luo told the envoy, "Go back and tell the Prince of Donghai: Youzhou is too cramped to hold an imperial throne. He must rule from Guanzhong to inherit the Founding Emperor's legacy.

sentences.zh: 若能迎駕潼關者，當位為上公，爵歸本國。」

translations.literal: If he will welcome my carriage at Tong Pass, I shall grant him the rank of Duke Paramount and restore his original title."
translations.idiomatic: If he will welcome me at Tong Pass, I shall grant him the rank of Duke Paramount and restore his original title."

sentences.zh: 堅怒，遣左將軍武都竇沖及呂光帥步騎四萬討之；

translations.literal: Fu Jian in anger dispatched Left General Dou Chong of Wudu and Lü Guang at the head of forty thousand infantry and cavalry to suppress him;
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Fu Jian dispatched Left General Dou Chong of Wudu and Lü Guang at the head of forty thousand infantry and cavalry to suppress him;

sentences.zh: 右將軍都貴馳傳詣鄴，將冀州兵三萬為前鋒；

translations.literal: Right General Du Gui rode post-haste to Ye to lead thirty thousand troops of Jizhou as vanguard;
translations.idiomatic: Right General Du Gui rode post-haste to Ye to lead thirty thousand Jizhou troops as vanguard;

sentences.zh: 以陽平公融為征討大都督。

translations.literal: Duke Rong the Duke of Yangping was made Grand Commander-in-Chief for the punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Rong of Yangping was appointed Grand Commander-in-Chief of the punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 北海公重悉薊城之眾與洛會，屯中山，有眾十萬。

translations.literal: Duke Zhong of Beihai mustered all the forces of Ji and joined Luo, encamping at Zhongshan with a host of one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhong of Beihai mobilized all the forces of Ji and joined Luo, encamping at Zhongshan with one hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 五月，竇沖等與洛戰於中山，洛兵大敗，生擒洛，送長安。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Dou Chong and the others fought Luo at Zhongshan; Luo's troops were utterly defeated, Luo was captured alive, and sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Dou Chong and his forces fought Luo at Zhongshan. Luo's army was routed, Luo was captured alive, and sent to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 北海公重走還薊，呂光追斬之。

translations.literal: Duke Zhong of Beihai fled back to Ji; Lü Guang pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhong of Beihai fled back to Ji, where Lü Guang pursued and killed him.

sentences.zh: 屯騎校尉石越自東萊帥騎一萬，浮海襲和龍，斬平規，幽州悉平。

translations.literal: Colonel of Garrison Cavalry Shi Yue, from Donglai leading ten thousand horsemen, crossed the sea to strike Helong, beheaded Ping Gui, and Youzhou was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue, Colonel of Garrison Cavalry, led ten thousand horsemen from Donglai across the sea against Helong, beheaded Ping Gui, and pacified all of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 堅赦洛不誅，徙涼州之西海郡。

translations.literal: Fu Jian pardoned Luo without execution and exiled him to Xihai Commandery in Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian spared Luo's life and exiled him to Xihai Commandery in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：夫有功不賞，有罪不誅，雖堯、舜不能為治，況他人乎！

translations.literal: Your subject Guang says: If merit goes unrewarded and guilt unpunished, even Yao and Shun could not govern well — how much less other men!
translations.idiomatic: Master Guang remarks: When merit goes unrewarded and guilt unpunished, not even Yao and Shun could govern well — how much less ordinary rulers!

sentences.zh: 秦王堅每得反者輒宥之，使其臣狃於為逆，行險徼幸，雖力屈被擒，猶不憂死，亂何自而息哉！

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin, whenever he captured rebels, always pardoned them, causing his subjects to grow accustomed to rebellion — they took to risky paths hoping for luck; even when their strength failed and they were captured, they still did not fear death. How was disorder ever to cease!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever King Fu Jian captured a rebel he pardoned him, accustoming his subjects to treason. Men took to desperate gambles; even when defeated and captured, they did not fear death. How could rebellion ever end?

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「威克厥愛，允濟；

translations.literal: The Documents say: "When awe overcomes affection, things are truly accomplished;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "When stern justice overcomes tender feeling, the task succeeds;

sentences.zh: 愛克厥威，允罔功。」

translations.literal: when affection overcomes awe, truly no achievement is made."
translations.idiomatic: when tender feeling overcomes stern justice, no achievement is made."

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「毋縱詭隨，以謹罔極；

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Do not indulge the deceitful and frivolous, lest lawlessness reach its extreme;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, "Do not indulge the deceitful and frivolous, lest lawlessness run rampant;

sentences.zh: 式遏寇虐，無俾作慝。」

translations.literal: check the brigand and the cruel — do not let them do evil."
translations.idiomatic: restrain violence and cruelty, and permit no wickedness."

sentences.zh: 今堅違之，能無亡乎！

translations.literal: Now Fu Jian violates these precepts — can he fail to perish!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian has violated these precepts — can ruin be far away?

sentences.zh: 朝廷以秦兵之退為謝安、桓沖之功，拜安衛將軍，與沖皆開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: The court credited the withdrawal of Qin troops to the merits of Xie An and Huan Chong; An was appointed General Who Guards the Realm, and both he and Chong received privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court credited the withdrawal of Qin troops to Xie An and Huan Chong; Xie An was made General Who Guards the Realm, and both he and Huan Chong received privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲子，大赦。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiazi, there was a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiazi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以會稽王道子為司徒；

translations.literal: On dingmao, the Prince of Kuaiji Sima Daozi was made Minister over the Masses;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Prince Daozi of Kuaiji was appointed Minister over the Masses;

sentences.zh: 固讓不拜。

translations.literal: he repeatedly declined and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: he repeatedly declined and refused the post.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅召陽平公融為侍中、中書監、都督中外諸軍事、車騎大將軍、司隸校尉、錄尚書事；

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin summoned Duke Rong of Yangping to serve as Palace Attendant, Director of the Palace Library, Commander of all Military Affairs within and without, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Colonel Director of Retainers, and Supervisor of Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian recalled Duke Rong of Yangping as Palace Attendant, Director of the Palace Library, supreme commander of military affairs within and without, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Colonel Director of Retainers, and Supervisor of Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 以征南大將軍、守尚書令長樂公丕為都督關東諸軍事、征東大將軍、冀州牧。

translations.literal: Great General on Southern Expedition, Acting Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke Pi of Changle was made Commander of all Military Affairs East of the Passes, Great General on Eastern Expedition, and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Pi of Changle, Great General on Southern Expedition and Acting Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed commander of military affairs east of the passes, Great General on Eastern Expedition, and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 堅以諸氐種類繁滋，秋，七月，分三原、九嵕、武都、汧、雍氐十五萬戶，使諸宗親各領之，散居方鎮，如古諸侯。

translations.literal: Fu Jian, because the Di tribes had multiplied greatly, in autumn, in the seventh month, distributed one hundred fifty thousand Di households from Sanyuan, Jiu'ao, Wudu, Qian, and Yong among various kinsmen to command, scattering them among the frontier garrisons like the feudal lords of old.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Di tribes had greatly multiplied, in autumn, the seventh month, Fu Jian distributed one hundred fifty thousand Di households from Sanyuan, Jiu'ao, Wudu, Qian, and Yong among his kinsmen to command, scattering them through the frontier garrisons like the feudal lords of old.

sentences.zh: 長樂公丕領氐三千戶，以仇池氐酋射聲校尉楊膺為征東左司馬，九嵕氐酋長水校尉齊午為右司馬，各領一千五百戶，為長樂世卿。

translations.literal: Duke Pi of Changle received three thousand Di households; She Sheng Colonel Yang Ying, chieftain of the Qiu Chi Di, was made Left Chief Military Aide on the Eastern Expedition, and Chang Shui Colonel Qi Wu, chieftain of the Jiu'ao Di, Right Chief Military Aide — each commanding fifteen hundred households as hereditary ministers of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Pi of Changle received three thousand Di households; Yang Ying, chieftain of the Qiu Chi Di and Colonel of She Sheng, was made Left Chief Military Aide on the Eastern Expedition, and Qi Wu, chieftain of the Jiu'ao Di and Chang Shui Colonel, Right Chief Military Aide — each commanding fifteen hundred households as hereditary ministers of Changle.

sentences.zh: 長樂國郎中令略陽垣敞為錄事參軍，侍講扶風韋干為參軍事，申紹為別駕。

translations.literal: Yuan Chang, Commandant of Officials of the State of Changle and a man of Lueyang, was made Recording Secretary; Wei Gan of Fufeng, Lecturer-in-Attendance, was made Military Aide; Shen Shao was made Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chang, Commandant of Officials of the State of Changle, was made Recording Secretary; Wei Gan of Fufeng, Court Lecturer, Military Aide; and Shen Shao Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 膺，丕之妃兄也；

translations.literal: Ying was Pi's elder brother-in-law;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ying was Pi's brother-in-law;

sentences.zh: 午，膺之妻父也。

translations.literal: Wu was Ying's father-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wu was Yang Ying's father-in-law.

sentences.zh: 八月，分幽州置平州，以石越為平州刺史，鎮龍城。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Pingzhou was carved from Youzhou; Shi Yue was made Inspector of Pingzhou and garrisoned Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Pingzhou was established from Youzhou; Shi Yue was appointed its inspector and garrisoned Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 中書令梁讜為幽州刺史，鎮薊城。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Liang Dang was made Inspector of Youzhou and garrisoned Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Dang, Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Inspector of Youzhou and garrisoned Ji.

sentences.zh: 撫軍將軍毛興為都督河、秦二州諸軍事、河州刺史，鎮枹罕。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Army Mao Xing was made Commander of all Military Affairs in He and Qin provinces, Governor of Hezhou, and garrisoned Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xing, General Who Pacifies the Army, was appointed commander of military affairs in He and Qin provinces, Governor of Hezhou, and garrisoned Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 長水校尉王騰為并州刺史，鎮晉陽。

translations.literal: Chang Shui Colonel Wang Teng was made Inspector of Bingzhou and garrisoned Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Teng, Chang Shui Colonel, was made Inspector of Bingzhou and garrisoned Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 河、并二州各配氐戶三千。

translations.literal: He and Bing provinces were each allotted three thousand Di households.
translations.idiomatic: He and Bing provinces were each assigned three thousand Di households.

sentences.zh: 興、騰並苻氏婚姻，氐之崇望也。

translations.literal: Xing and Teng were both connected to the Fu clan by marriage and were eminent men among the Di.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xing and Wang Teng were both connected to the Fu clan by marriage and were eminent among the Di.

sentences.zh: 平原公暉為都督豫、洛、荊、南兗、東豫、揚六州諸軍事、鎮東大將軍、豫州牧，鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: Duke Hui of Pingyuan was made Commander of all Military Affairs in the six provinces of Yu, Luo, Jing, Southern Yan, Eastern Yu, and Yang, Great General Who Guards the East, Governor of Yuzhou, and garrisoned Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Hui of Pingyuan was made supreme commander of military affairs in Yu, Luo, Jing, Southern Yan, Eastern Yu, and Yang provinces, Great General Who Guards the East, Governor of Yuzhou, and garrisoned Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 移洛州刺史治豐陽。

translations.literal: The seat of the Inspector of Luozhou was moved to Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: The seat of the Inspector of Luozhou was moved to Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 以巨鹿公睿為雍州刺史，鎮蒲阪。

translations.literal: Duke Rui of Julu was made Inspector of Yongzhou and garrisoned Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Rui of Julu was made Inspector of Yongzhou and garrisoned Puban.

sentences.zh: 各配氐戶三千二百。

translations.literal: Each was allotted three thousand two hundred Di households.
translations.idiomatic: Each was assigned three thousand two hundred Di households.

sentences.zh: 堅送丕至灞上，諸氐別其父兄，皆慟哭，哀感路人。

translations.literal: Fu Jian escorted Pi as far as Bashang; when the Di people parted from their fathers and elder brothers, all wept bitterly — their grief moved passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian escorted Pi as far as Bashang. When the Di people parted from their fathers and brothers, all wept bitterly, moving passersby to tears.

sentences.zh: 趙整因侍宴，援琴而歌曰：「阿得脂，阿得脂，博勞舅父是仇綏，尾長翼短不能飛。

translations.literal: Zhao Zheng, while attending a banquet, took up a zither and sang: "A-de-zhi, a-de-zhi — the shrike's maternal uncle is Qiu Sui; his tail is long and wings short, he cannot fly.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Zhao Zheng took up a zither and sang: "A-de-zhi, a-de-zhi — the shrike's maternal uncle is Qiu Sui; his tail is long, his wings short — he cannot fly.

sentences.zh: 遠徙種人留鮮卑，一旦緩急當語誰！」

translations.literal: You exile your own people far away yet leave the Xianbei behind — when crisis comes, whom will you call upon!"
translations.idiomatic: You send your own people far away while the Xianbei remain behind — when crisis comes, whom will you call upon!"

sentences.zh: 堅笑而不納。

translations.literal: Fu Jian laughed and did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian laughed it off and paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸未，皇后王氏崩。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guiwei, Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guiwei, Empress Wang died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，九真太守李遜據交州反。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, Administrator Li Xun of Jiuzhen seized Jiaozhou and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Li Xun, Administrator of Jiuzhen, seized Jiaozhou and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅以左禁將軍楊壁為秦州刺史，尚書趙遷為洛州刺史，南巴校尉姜宇為寧州刺史。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin made Left Guard General Yang Bi Governor of Qinzhou, Master of Writing Zhao Qian Governor of Luozhou, and Colonel of Southern Ba Jiang Yu Governor of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian appointed Left Guard General Yang Bi Governor of Qinzhou, Master of Writing Zhao Qian Governor of Luozhou, and Jiang Yu, Colonel of Southern Ba, Governor of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙酉，葬定皇后於隆平陵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yiyou, Empress Ding was buried at Longping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yiyou, Empress Ding was interred at Longping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 十二月，秦以左將軍都貴為荊州刺史，鎮彭城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Qin made Left General Du Gui Inspector of Jingzhou and garrisoned Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Qin appointed Left General Du Gui Inspector of Jingzhou, with his command at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 置東豫州，以毛當為刺史，鎮許昌。

translations.literal: Eastern Yuzhou was established; Mao Dang was made its inspector and garrisoned Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Yuzhou was established; Mao Dang was made its inspector and garrisoned Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，秦王堅遣高密太守毛璪之等二百餘人來歸。

translations.literal: This year, King Fu Jian of Qin sent Mao Qianzhi, Administrator of Gaomi, and more than two hundred others to surrender to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: That year, King Fu Jian sent Mao Qianzhi, Administrator of Gaomi, and more than two hundred others to defect to Jin.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝上之中太元六年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — sixth year of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — sixth year of Taiyuan (

sentences.zh: 辛巳，公元三八一年）

translations.literal: xinsi, corresponding to 381 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinsi year, 381 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，帝初奉佛法，立精舍於殿內，引諸沙門居之。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, the emperor for the first time embraced Buddhist teachings, established a meditation hall within the palace, and invited monks to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the emperor embraced Buddhism for the first time, built a monastery within the palace, and invited monks to live there.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞王雅表諫，不從。

translations.literal: Wang Ya, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, submitted a memorial of remonstrance; the emperor did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, submitted a memorial of remonstrance, but the emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 雅，肅之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Ya was the great-grandson of Su.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya was the great-grandson of Wang Su.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以尚書謝石為僕射。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Xie Shi of the Masters of Writing was made Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Xie Shi was appointed Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 二月，東夷，西域六十二國入貢於秦。

translations.literal: In the second month, sixty-two states of the Eastern Yi and the Western Regions brought tribute to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, sixty-two states of the Eastern Yi and the Western Regions presented tribute to Qin.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，庚子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, in the sixth month, on the first day gengzi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, on the first day (gengzi), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲午，交趾太守杜瑗斬李遜，交州平。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on jiawu, Administrator Du Yuan of Jiaozhi beheaded Li Xun and Jiaozhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiawu, Du Yuan, Administrator of Jiaozhi, beheaded Li Xun and pacified Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，故武陵王晞卒於新安，追封新寧郡王，命其子遵為嗣。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, the former Prince of Wuling Xi died at Xin'an; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Xinning Commandery, and his son Zun was ordered to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, the former Prince of Wuling, Xi, died at Xin'an; he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Xinning Commandery, and his son Zun was named his heir.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己亥，以前會稽內史郗愔為司空；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jihai, the former Interior Minister Chi Yin of Kuaiji was made Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jihai, Chi Yin, former Interior Minister of Kuaiji, was appointed Minister of Works;

sentences.zh: 愔固辭不起。

translations.literal: Yin firmly declined and would not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Yin firmly declined and refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 秦荊州刺史都貴遣其司馬閻振、中兵參軍吳仲帥眾二萬寇竟陵，桓沖遣南平太守桓石虔、衛軍參軍桓石民等帥水陸二萬拒之。

translations.literal: Qin's Inspector of Jingzhou Du Gui dispatched his Chief Military Aide Yan Zhen and Central Army Aide Wu Zhong at the head of twenty thousand men to raid Jingling; Huan Chong sent Administrator of Nanping Huan Shiqian and Army Aide of the Guard Huan Shimin and others at the head of twenty thousand men by land and water to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Du Gui, Qin's Inspector of Jingzhou, sent his Chief Military Aide Yan Zhen and Central Army Aide Wu Zhong with twenty thousand men to raid Jingling. Huan Chong dispatched Huan Shiqian, Administrator of Nanping, and Huan Shimin, Army Aide of the Guard, with twenty thousand troops by land and water to resist them.

sentences.zh: 石民，石虔之弟也。

translations.literal: Shimin was Shiqian's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin was Shiqian's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲辰，石虔襲擊振、仲，大破之，振、仲退保管城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiachen, Shiqian launched a surprise attack on Zhen and Zhong, utterly defeating them; Zhen and Zhong retreated to hold Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiachen, Shiqian launched a surprise attack on Zhen and Zhong and routed them; Zhen and Zhong retreated to hold Guancheng.

sentences.zh: 石虔進攻之，癸亥，拔管城，獲振、仲，斬首七千級，俘虜萬人。

translations.literal: Shiqian pressed the attack; on guihai, he took Guancheng, captured Zhen and Zhong, beheaded seven thousand, and took ten thousand prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian pressed the attack and, on guihai, captured Guancheng, taking Zhen and Zhong prisoner, beheading seven thousand, and capturing ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 詔封桓沖子謙為宜陽侯，以桓石虔領河東太守。

translations.literal: An edict enfeoffed Huan Chong's son Qian as Marquis of Yiyang and made Huan Shiqian acting Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed Huan Chong's son Qian as Marquis of Yiyang and made Huan Shiqian acting Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 是歲，江東大饑。

translations.literal: This year the lands east of the Yangtze suffered great famine.
translations.idiomatic: That year the lands east of the Yangtze suffered a great famine.

sentences.zh: 烈宗孝武皇帝上之中太元七年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — seventh year of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liefu line, upper fascicle, middle section — seventh year of Taiyuan (

sentences.zh: 壬午，公元三八二年）

translations.literal: renwu, corresponding to 382 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renwu year, 382 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，三月，秦大司農東海公陽、員外散騎侍郎王皮、尚書郎周颺謀反，事覺，收下廷尉。

translations.literal: In spring, in the third month, Qin's Grand Minister of Agriculture Duke Yang of Donghai, Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant Wang Pi, and Master of Writing Zhou Yang plotted rebellion; the affair was discovered and they were arrested and handed over to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the third month, Duke Yang of Donghai, Qin's Grand Minister of Agriculture, Wang Pi, Supernumerary Gentleman Attendant, and Zhou Yang, Master of Writing, plotted rebellion. The plot was discovered and they were arrested and handed over to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 陽，法之子；

translations.literal: Yang was the son of Fa;
translations.idiomatic: Yang was the son of Fu Fa;

sentences.zh: 皮，猛之子也。

translations.literal: Pi was the son of Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi was the son of Wang Meng.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅問其反狀，陽曰：「臣父哀公死不以罪，臣為父復仇耳。」

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin asked them the circumstances of their rebellion. Yang said: "My father Duke Ai died without having committed a crime — I am avenging my father, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian questioned them about their rebellion. Yang said, "My father Duke Ai died without having committed any crime — I am avenging my father, that is all."

sentences.zh: 堅泣曰：「哀公之死，事不在朕，卿豈不知之！」

translations.literal: Fu Jian wept and said: "Duke Ai's death was not my doing — do you not know this!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian wept and said, "Duke Ai's death was not my doing — surely you know that!"

sentences.zh: 王皮曰：「臣父丞相，有佐命之勳，而臣不免貧賤，故欲圖富貴耳。」

translations.literal: Wang Pi said: "My father was chief minister and had the merit of aiding in the founding of the state, yet I could not escape poverty and low station — so I sought wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi said, "My father was chief minister and had the merit of founding the state, yet I remained poor and obscure — so I sought wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「丞相臨終托卿，以十具牛為治田之資，未嘗為卿求官。

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "When the chief minister was dying he entrusted you with ten teams of oxen as capital for farming — he never sought office for you.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "When your father was dying he left you ten teams of oxen as capital for farming — he never asked me to give you office.

sentences.zh: 知子莫若父，何其明也！」

translations.literal: No one knows a son like his father — how perceptive he was!"
translations.idiomatic: No one knows a son like his father — how perceptive he was!"

sentences.zh: 周颺曰：「颺世荷晉恩，生為晉鬼，復何問乎！」

translations.literal: Zhou Yang said: "Yang's family has long owed Jin a debt of grace — in life I was Jin's man, in death I shall be Jin's ghost. What more is there to ask!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yang said, "My family has long owed Jin a debt of grace — in life I was Jin's man, in death I shall be Jin's ghost. What more is there to ask?

sentences.zh: 先是，颺屢謀反叛，左右皆請殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang had repeatedly plotted rebellion, and those around him all asked that he be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang had repeatedly plotted rebellion, and his attendants all urged that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「孟威烈士，秉志如此，豈憚死乎！

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "Meng Wei is a man of heroic resolve — with such steadfast purpose, would he fear death?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "Meng Wei is a man of heroic resolve — with such steadfast purpose, would he fear death?

sentences.zh: 殺之適足成其名耳！」

translations.literal: To kill him would only complete his fame!"
translations.idiomatic: To kill him would only make him a martyr!"

sentences.zh: 皆赦，不誅，徙陽於涼州之高昌郡，皮、颺於朔方之北。

translations.literal: All were pardoned without execution: Yang was exiled to Gaochang Commandery in Liangzhou, Pi and Yang to the far north of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: All were pardoned: Yang was exiled to Gaochang Commandery in Liangzhou, Pi and Yang to the far north of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 颺卒於朔方。

translations.literal: Yang died in Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yang died in Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 陽勇力兼人，尋復徙鄯善。

translations.literal: Yang was a man of combined courage and strength; before long he was again transferred to Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yang was a man of great courage and strength; before long he was transferred again to Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 及建元之末，秦國大亂，陽劫鄯善之相，欲求東歸，鄯善王殺之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianyuan era, when Qin fell into great disorder, Yang seized the prime minister of Shanshan, seeking to return east; the King of Shanshan killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jianyuan era, when Qin fell into chaos, Yang seized the prime minister of Shanshan in an attempt to return east; the King of Shanshan killed him.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅徙鄴銅駝、銅馬、飛廉、翁仲於長安。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin moved the bronze camel, bronze horse, Flying General, and Weng Zhong statues from Ye to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian moved the bronze camel, bronze horse, Flying General, and Weng Zhong statues from Ye to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，堅扶風太守王永為幽刺史。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Fu Jian made Wang Yong, Administrator of Fufeng, Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Fu Jian appointed Wang Yong, Administrator of Fufeng, Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 永，皮之兄也。

translations.literal: Yong was Pi's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yong was Wang Pi's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 皮凶險無行，而永清修好學，故堅用之。

translations.literal: Pi was fierce, treacherous, and without proper conduct, whereas Yong was pure, cultivated, and fond of learning — therefore Fu Jian employed Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi was fierce, treacherous, and dissolute, whereas Wang Yong was upright, cultivated, and fond of learning — therefore Fu Jian employed Yong.

sentences.zh: 以陽平公融為司徒，融固辭不受。

translations.literal: Duke Rong of Yangping was made Minister over the Masses, but Rong firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Rong of Yangping was appointed Minister over the Masses, but Rong firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 堅方謀伐晉，乃以融為征南大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Fu Jian was then planning to attack Jin, and so made Rong Great General on Southern Expedition with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was planning to attack Jin, and so made Rong Great General on Southern Expedition with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 五月，幽州蝗生，廣袤千里。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, locusts appeared in Youzhou, covering a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, locusts appeared in Youzhou, covering a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅使散騎常侍彭城劉蘭發幽、冀、青、并民撲除之。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin sent Regular Attendant Liu Lan of Pengcheng to mobilize the people of You, Ji, Qing, and Bing provinces to exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian sent Liu Lan of Pengcheng, Regular Attendant, to mobilize the people of You, Ji, Qing, and Bing provinces to exterminate them.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，癸卯，大赦。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, on guimao, there was a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on guimao, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅以諫方大夫裴元略為巴西、樟潼二郡太守，使密具舟師。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin made Remonstrance Officer Pei Yuanlue Administrator of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zhangtong, ordering him secretly to prepare a fleet.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian made Pei Yuanlue, Remonstrance Officer, Administrator of Baxi and Zhangtong commanderies, ordering him secretly to prepare a fleet.

sentences.zh: 九月，車師前部王彌窴、鄯善王休密馱入朝於秦，請為鄉導，以伐西域之不服者，因如漢法置都護以統理之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Mi Tuo, King of the Front Division of Cheshi, and Xiumituo, King of Shanshan, came to court in Qin, requesting to serve as guides to attack those in the Western Regions who would not submit, and to establish a Protector-General to govern them according to Han precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Mi Tuo, King of the Front Division of Cheshi, and Xiumituo, King of Shanshan, came to court in Qin, offering to serve as guides against the unsubmissive states of the Western Regions and to establish a Protector-General to govern them on the Han model.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅以驍騎將軍呂光為使持節、都督西域征討諸軍事，與凌江將軍姜飛、輕車將軍彭晃、將軍杜進、康盛等總兵十萬，鐵騎五千，以伐西域。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin made General of Fierce Cavalry Lü Guang Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Commander of all Military Affairs for the Punitive Expedition in the Western Regions, and together with General Who Crosses the River Jiang Fei, General of Light Chariots Peng Huang, and Generals Du Jin and Kang Sheng and others commanded one hundred thousand troops and five thousand iron cavalry to attack the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian made Lü Guang, General of Fierce Cavalry, Bearer of the Staff of Authority and supreme commander of the punitive expedition in the Western Regions. Together with Jiang Fei, General Who Crosses the River, Peng Huang, General of Light Chariots, and Generals Du Jin and Kang Sheng, he commanded one hundred thousand troops and five thousand iron cavalry against the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 陽平公融諫曰：「西域荒遠，得其民不可使，得其地不可食，漢武征之，得不補失。

translations.literal: Duke Rong of Yangping remonstrated: "The Western Regions are remote and barren — their people, once obtained, cannot be employed; their lands, once obtained, cannot feed us. Emperor Wu of Han campaigned there and gained less than he lost.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Rong of Yangping remonstrated, "The Western Regions are remote and barren — their people cannot be employed and their lands cannot feed us. Emperor Wu of Han campaigned there and gained less than he lost.

sentences.zh: 今勞師萬里之外，以踵漢氏之過舉，臣竊惜之。」

translations.literal: Now to weary the army ten thousand li away, repeating the Han dynasty's mistaken enterprise — I deeply regret this."
translations.idiomatic: To weary the army ten thousand li away, repeating the Han dynasty's mistake — I deeply regret it.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: Fu Jian did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian would not listen.

sentences.zh: 桓沖使揚威將軍朱綽擊秦荊州刺史都貴於襄陽，焚踐沔北屯田，掠六百餘戶而還。

translations.literal: Huan Chong sent General Who Displays Might Zhu Chuo to attack Qin's Inspector of Jingzhou Du Gui at Xiangyang, burning and ravaging the garrison farms north of the Mian River and carrying off more than six hundred households before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong sent Zhu Chuo, General Who Displays Might, to attack Du Gui, Qin's Inspector of Jingzhou, at Xiangyang, burning the garrison farms north of the Mian River and carrying off more than six hundred households before returning.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，秦王堅會群臣於太極殿，議曰：「自吾承業，垂三十載，四方略定，唯東南一隅，未沾王化。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, King Fu Jian of Qin assembled his ministers in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and said: "Since I inherited the enterprise, nearly thirty years have passed; the four quarters are largely settled — only the southeastern corner has not yet received royal transformation.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, King Fu Jian assembled his ministers in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and said, "Since I inherited the throne, nearly thirty years have passed. The four quarters are largely settled — only the southeast has not yet submitted to our rule.

sentences.zh: 今略計吾士卒，可得九十七萬，吾欲自將以討之，何如？」

translations.literal: By rough count my soldiers number nine hundred seventy thousand. I wish to lead them in person to suppress Jin — what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: By rough count my soldiers number nine hundred seventy thousand. I wish to lead them in person against Jin — what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 秘書監朱肜曰：「陛下返中國士民，使復其桑梓，然後回輿東巡，告成岱宗，此千載一時也！」

translations.literal: Privy Treasurer Zhu Rong said: "Your Majesty should return the Chinese people to their native places and restore their ancestral homes, then turn your carriage east to tour the realm and announce your achievement at Mount Tai — this is a once-in-a-thousand-years opportunity!"
translations.idiomatic: Privy Treasurer Zhu Rong said, "Your Majesty should return the Chinese people to their native places, then turn your carriage east to tour the realm and announce your achievement at Mount Tai — this is a once-in-a-thousand-years opportunity!"

sentences.zh: 堅喜曰：「是吾志也。」

translations.literal: Fu Jian said with pleasure: "That is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said with pleasure, "That is my wish."

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射權翼曰：「昔紂為無道，三仁在朝，武王猶為之旋師。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Quan Yi said: "In antiquity King Zhou of Shang was without the Way, yet three worthies served in his court — still King Wu turned his army back.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Yi, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, said, "In antiquity King Zhou of Shang was without the Way, yet three worthies served in his court — still King Wu turned his army back.

sentences.zh: 今晉雖微弱，未有大惡。

translations.literal: Now though Jin is weak, it has committed no great evil.
translations.idiomatic: Now though Jin is weak, it has committed no great evil.

sentences.zh: 謝安、桓沖皆江表偉人，君臣輯睦，內外同心。

translations.literal: Xie An and Huan Chong are both great men south of the Yangtze; ruler and ministers are harmonious, inner and outer united in purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An and Huan Chong are both great men south of the Yangtze; ruler and ministers are harmonious and united within and without.

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，未可圖也。」

translations.literal: In my view, they cannot be taken."
translations.idiomatic: In my view, they cannot be taken."

sentences.zh: 堅嘿然良久，曰：「諸君各言其志。」

translations.literal: Fu Jian was silent for a long while, then said: "Let each of you speak his mind."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was silent for a long while, then said, "Let each of you speak his mind."

sentences.zh: 太子左衛率石越曰：「今歲鎮守鬥，福德在吳。

translations.literal: Left Guard Leader of the Crown Prince Shi Yue said: "This year the Guardian Star is in Wu's quarter and fortune rests with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue, Left Guard Leader of the Crown Prince, said, "This year the Guardian Star is in Wu's quarter and fortune rests with Wu.

sentences.zh: 伐之，必有天殃。

translations.literal: To attack them will surely bring heavenly calamity.
translations.idiomatic: To attack them will surely bring heavenly calamity.

sentences.zh: 且彼據長江之險，民為之用，殆未可伐也！」

translations.literal: Moreover they hold the Yangtze's natural defenses and the people serve them — they can scarcely be attacked!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they hold the Yangtze's natural defenses and the people serve them — they can scarcely be attacked!"

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「昔武王伐紂，逆歲違卜。

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "When King Wu attacked Zhou, he went against the year-star and defied the oracle.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "When King Wu attacked Zhou, he went against the year-star and defied the oracle.

sentences.zh: 天道幽遠，未易可知。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven is deep and remote — it is not easily known.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of Heaven is deep and remote — it is not easily known.

sentences.zh: 夫差、孫皓皆保據江湖，不免於亡。

translations.literal: Fuchai of Wu and Sun Hao both held the rivers and lakes yet could not escape destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchai of Wu and Sun Hao both held the rivers and lakes yet could not escape destruction.

sentences.zh: 今以吾之眾，投鞭於江，足斷其流，又何險之足恃乎！」

translations.literal: Now with my multitude, if we cast whips into the river, they would suffice to dam its flow — what defense is worth relying on!"
translations.idiomatic: Now with my multitude, if we cast whips into the river, they would suffice to dam its flow — what defense is worth relying on!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「三國之君皆淫虐無道，故敵國取之，易於拾遺。

translations.literal: Shi Yue replied: "The rulers of the Three Kingdoms were all licentious and tyrannical without the Way — therefore enemy states took them as easily as picking up something dropped on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue replied, "The rulers of the Three Kingdoms were all licentious and tyrannical — therefore enemy states took them as easily as picking up something dropped on the road.

sentences.zh: 今晉雖無德，未有大罪，願陛下且案兵積穀，以待其釁。」

translations.literal: Now though Jin lacks virtue, it has committed no great crime. Your Majesty, please hold the army and accumulate grain, waiting for their fault to appear."
translations.idiomatic: Now though Jin lacks virtue, it has committed no great crime. Your Majesty, please hold the army and accumulate grain, waiting for their fault to appear."

sentences.zh: 於是群臣各言利害，久之不決。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ministers each spoke of advantage and harm, and for a long time no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the ministers each spoke of advantage and harm, and for a long time no decision was reached.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「此所謂築室道旁，無時可成。

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "This is what is called building a house beside the road — it can never be finished.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "This is what is called building a house beside the road — it can never be finished.

sentences.zh: 吾當內斷於心耳！」

translations.literal: I shall decide within my own heart!"
translations.idiomatic: I shall decide within my own heart!"

sentences.zh: 群臣皆出，獨留陽平公融，謂之曰：「自古定大事者，不過一二臣而已。

translations.literal: When all the ministers had withdrawn, Fu Jian kept Duke Rong of Yangping alone and said to him: "Since antiquity, those who settle great affairs have never been more than one or two ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When all the ministers had withdrawn, Fu Jian kept Duke Rong of Yangping alone and said, "Since antiquity, those who settle great affairs have never been more than one or two ministers.

sentences.zh: 今眾言紛紛，徒亂人意，吾當與汝決之。」

translations.literal: Now the multitude of voices only confuses the mind — I shall decide this with you."
translations.idiomatic: Now the multitude of voices only confuses the mind — I shall decide this with you."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「今伐晉有三難：天道不順，一也；

translations.literal: Rong replied: "To attack Jin now presents three difficulties: the Way of Heaven is not favorable — that is the first;
translations.idiomatic: Rong replied, "To attack Jin now presents three difficulties: the Way of Heaven is not favorable — that is the first;

sentences.zh: 晉國無釁，二也；

translations.literal: Jin has given no cause for attack — that is the second;
translations.idiomatic: Jin has given no cause for attack — that is the second;

sentences.zh: 我數戰兵疲，民有畏敵之心，三也。

translations.literal: we have fought repeatedly and the army is weary, and the people fear the enemy — that is the third.
translations.idiomatic: we have fought repeatedly and the army is weary, and the people fear the enemy — that is the third.

sentences.zh: 群臣言晉不可伐者，皆忠臣也，願陛下聽之。」

translations.literal: Those ministers who say Jin cannot be attacked are all loyal subjects — Your Majesty, please heed them."
translations.idiomatic: Those ministers who say Jin cannot be attacked are all loyal subjects — Your Majesty, please heed them."

sentences.zh: 堅作色曰：「汝亦如此，吾復何望！

translations.literal: Fu Jian changed color and said: "You too speak thus — what hope have I left!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's face darkened and he said, "You too speak thus — what hope have I left!

sentences.zh: 吾強兵百萬，資仗如山；

translations.literal: I have a mighty army of one million and supplies and weapons like mountains;
translations.idiomatic: I have a mighty army of one million and supplies and weapons like mountains;
