sentences.zh: 吾雖未為令主，亦非暗劣。

translations.literal: though I am not yet a perfect ruler, I am not dim-witted either.
translations.idiomatic: though I am not yet a perfect ruler, I am not dim-witted either.

sentences.zh: 乘累捷之勢，擊垂亡之國，何患不克，豈可復留此殘寇，使長為國家之憂哉！」

translations.literal: Riding the momentum of repeated victories to strike a state on the verge of collapse — what worry is there of failure? How can we leave this remnant foe to be a perpetual worry to the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Riding the momentum of repeated victories to strike a state on the verge of collapse — what worry is there of failure? How can we leave this remnant foe to be a perpetual worry to the state!"

sentences.zh: 融泣曰：「晉未可滅，昭然甚明。

translations.literal: Rong wept and said: "That Jin cannot be destroyed is abundantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wept and said, "That Jin cannot be destroyed is abundantly clear.

sentences.zh: 今勞師大舉，恐無萬全之功。

translations.literal: Now to launch a great campaign — I fear there will be no guarantee of complete success.
translations.idiomatic: Now to launch a great campaign — I fear there will be no guarantee of complete success.

sentences.zh: 且臣之所憂，不止於此。

translations.literal: And my worry is not limited to this alone.
translations.idiomatic: And my worry is not limited to this alone.

sentences.zh: 陛下寵育鮮卑、羌、羯，佈滿畿甸，此屬皆我之深仇。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has nurtured and favored the Xianbei, Qiang, and Jie, scattering them throughout the capital region — these are all our deepest enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has nurtured and favored the Xianbei, Qiang, and Jie, scattering them throughout the capital region — these are all our deepest enemies.

sentences.zh: 太子獨與弱卒數萬留守京師，臣懼有不虞之變生於腹心肘掖，不可悔也。

translations.literal: The crown prince alone with a few tens of thousands of weak troops remains to guard the capital — I fear some unforeseen change may arise at the very heart of the realm, beyond recall.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince alone with a few tens of thousands of weak troops remains to guard the capital — I fear some unforeseen change may arise at the very heart of the realm, beyond recall.

sentences.zh: 臣之頑愚，誠不足采；

translations.literal: My stubborn foolishness is truly unworthy of consideration;
translations.idiomatic: My stubborn foolishness is truly unworthy of consideration;

sentences.zh: 王景略一時英傑，陛下常比之諸葛武侯，獨不記其臨沒之言乎！」

translations.literal: Wang Jinglue was a hero of his age — Your Majesty often compared him to Zhuge Liang — have you alone forgotten his dying words!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jinglue was a hero of his age — Your Majesty often compared him to Zhuge Liang — have you alone forgotten his dying words!"

sentences.zh: 堅不聽。

translations.literal: Fu Jian did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian would not listen.

sentences.zh: 於是朝臣進諫者眾，堅曰：「以吾擊晉，校其強弱之勢，猶疾風之掃秋葉，而朝廷內外皆言不可，誠吾所不解也！」

translations.literal: Many court ministers then came forward to remonstrate. Fu Jian said: "When I compare my strength with Jin's, attacking Jin is like a fierce wind sweeping autumn leaves — yet within and without the court all say it cannot be done. Truly I cannot understand this!"
translations.idiomatic: Many court ministers then came forward to remonstrate. Fu Jian said, "When I compare my strength with Jin's, attacking Jin is like a fierce wind sweeping autumn leaves — yet within and without the court all say it cannot be done. Truly I cannot understand this!"

sentences.zh: 太子宏曰：「今歲在吳分，又晉君無罪，若大舉不捷，恐威名外挫，財力內竭，此群下所以疑也！」

translations.literal: Crown Prince Hong said: "This year the star is in Wu's quarter, and moreover the Jin ruler is without guilt — if a great campaign does not succeed, I fear our prestige will be shattered abroad and our resources exhausted at home. That is why your subjects doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Hong said, "This year the star is in Wu's quarter, and moreover the Jin ruler is without guilt — if a great campaign does not succeed, I fear our prestige will be shattered abroad and our resources exhausted at home. That is why your subjects doubt!"

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「昔吾滅燕，亦犯歲而捷，天道固難知也。

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "When I destroyed Yan, I too went against the year-star and yet succeeded — the Way of Heaven is indeed hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "When I destroyed Yan, I too went against the year-star and yet succeeded — the Way of Heaven is indeed hard to know.

sentences.zh: 秦滅六國，六國之君豈皆暴虐乎！」

translations.literal: When Qin destroyed the Six States, were all their rulers tyrannical!"
translations.idiomatic: When Qin destroyed the Six States, were all their rulers tyrannical!"

sentences.zh: 冠軍、京兆尹慕容垂言於堅曰：「弱並於強，小並於大，此理勢自然，非難知也。

translations.literal: Murong Chui, Champion of the Realm and Intendant of Jingzhao, said to Fu Jian: "The weak being absorbed by the strong, the small by the large — this is the natural course of reason and circumstance, not hard to understand.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui, Champion of the Realm and Intendant of Jingzhao, said to Fu Jian, "The weak being absorbed by the strong, the small by the large — this is the natural course of reason and circumstance, not hard to understand.

sentences.zh: 以陛下神武應期，威加海外，虎旅百萬，韓、白滿朝，而蕞爾江南，獨違王命，豈可復留之以遺子孫哉！

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's divine martial prowess answering the age, your authority extending beyond the seas, tiger troops numbering one million, and Han Xin and Bai Qi filling the court — yet this tiny land south of the Yangtze alone defies your command — how can we leave it to burden our descendants!
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's divine martial prowess answering the age, your authority extending beyond the seas, tiger troops numbering one million, and men like Han Xin and Bai Qi filling the court — yet this tiny land south of the Yangtze alone defies your command — how can we leave it to burden our descendants!

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『謀夫孔多，是用不集。』

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Counsellors are many, therefore nothing is accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, "Counsellors are many, therefore nothing is accomplished."

sentences.zh: 陛下斷自聖心足矣，何必廣詢朝眾！

translations.literal: Your Majesty need only decide from your sage heart — why consult the multitude of the court!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty need only decide from your sage heart — why consult the multitude of the court!

sentences.zh: 晉武平吳，所仗者張、杜二三臣而已，若從朝眾之言，豈有混壹之功乎！」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Jin pacified Wu, he relied on no more than two or three ministers like Zhang and Du — if he had followed the court's counsel, would he have achieved unification!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Jin pacified Wu, he relied on no more than two or three ministers like Zhang and Du — if he had followed the court's counsel, would he have achieved unification!"

sentences.zh: 堅大悅，曰：「與吾共定天下者，獨卿而已。」

translations.literal: Fu Jian was greatly pleased and said: "The one who will settle the realm with me is you alone."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was greatly pleased and said, "The one who will settle the realm with me is you alone."

sentences.zh: 賜帛五百匹。

translations.literal: He bestowed five hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed five hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 堅銳意欲取江東，寢不能旦。

translations.literal: Fu Jian was keenly intent on taking the lands east of the Yangtze and could scarcely sleep until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian was keenly intent on taking the lands east of the Yangtze and could scarcely sleep until dawn.

sentences.zh: 陽平公融諫曰：「『知足不辱，知止不殆。』

translations.literal: Duke Rong of Yangping remonstrated: ""To know sufficiency is not to be disgraced; to know when to stop is not to be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Rong of Yangping remonstrated, ""To know sufficiency is not to be disgraced; to know when to stop is not to be endangered.

sentences.zh: 自古窮兵極武，未有不亡者。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, those who exhaust the state in warfare have never failed to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, those who exhaust the state in warfare have never failed to perish.

sentences.zh: 且國家本戎狄也，正朔會不歸人。

translations.literal: Moreover our state is originally of the Rong and Di — the imperial calendar will surely not pass to us.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover our state is originally of the Rong and Di — the imperial calendar will surely not pass to us.

sentences.zh: 江東雖微弱僅存，然中華正統，天意必不絕之。」

translations.literal: The lands east of the Yangtze, though weak and barely surviving, are nevertheless the orthodox lineage of the Central States — Heaven's intent will surely not let it perish."
translations.idiomatic: The lands east of the Yangtze, though weak and barely surviving, are nevertheless the orthodox lineage of the Central States — Heaven's intent will surely not let it perish."

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「帝王歷數，豈有常邪！

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "The succession of emperors — can it be constant!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "The succession of emperors — can it be constant!

sentences.zh: 惟德之所在耳！

translations.literal: It depends only on where virtue resides!
translations.idiomatic: It depends only on where virtue resides!

sentences.zh: 劉禪豈非漢之苗裔邪，終為魏所滅。

translations.literal: Was Liu Shan not a descendant of Han? Yet in the end he was destroyed by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Was Liu Shan not a descendant of Han? Yet in the end he was destroyed by Wei.

sentences.zh: 汝所以不如吾者，正病此不達變通耳！」

translations.literal: The reason you are not my equal is precisely that you suffer from this failure to grasp change and adapt!"
translations.idiomatic: The reason you are not my equal is precisely that you suffer from this failure to grasp change and adapt!"

sentences.zh: 堅素信重沙門道安，群臣使道安乘間進言。

translations.literal: Fu Jian had long trusted and honored the Buddhist monk Dao An; the ministers had Dao An seize an opportune moment to offer counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian had long trusted and honored the Buddhist monk Dao An; the ministers had Dao An seize an opportune moment to offer counsel.

sentences.zh: 十一月，堅與道安同輦游於東苑，堅曰：「朕將與公南遊吳、越，泛長江，臨滄海，不亦樂乎！」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Fu Jian rode in the same carriage with Dao An touring the Eastern Park. Fu Jian said: "I shall travel south with you to Wu and Yue, sail the Long River, and stand before the blue sea — is this not joy!"
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Fu Jian rode in the same carriage with Dao An touring the Eastern Park. Fu Jian said, "I shall travel south with you to Wu and Yue, sail the Long River, and stand before the blue sea — is this not joy!"

sentences.zh: 安曰：「陛下應天御世，居中土而制四維，自足比隆堯、舜，何必櫛風沐雨，經略遐方乎！

translations.literal: Dao An said: "Your Majesty responds to Heaven and governs the age, holding the central lands and controlling the four directions — this alone suffices to match the glory of Yao and Shun. Why must you comb the wind and wash in the rain, campaigning in distant regions!
translations.idiomatic: Dao An said, "Your Majesty responds to Heaven and governs the age, holding the central lands and controlling the four directions — this alone suffices to match the glory of Yao and Shun. Why must you comb the wind and wash in the rain, campaigning in distant regions!

sentences.zh: 且東南卑濕，沴氣易構，虞舜游而不歸，大禹往而不復。

translations.literal: Moreover the southeast is low and damp, and pestilential vapors easily arise — Emperor Shun toured there and did not return; Yu the Great went there and did not come back.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the southeast is low and damp, and pestilential vapors easily arise — Emperor Shun toured there and did not return; Yu the Great went there and did not come back.

sentences.zh: 何足以上勞大駕也！」

translations.literal: How can it be worth troubling the imperial carriage for this!"
translations.idiomatic: How can it be worth troubling the imperial carriage for this!"

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「天生烝民，而樹之君，使司牧之，朕豈敢憚勞，使彼一方獨不被澤乎！

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "Heaven produced the multitude and established rulers over them to govern and shepherd the people — how dare I shrink from toil and leave that one region alone without my grace!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "Heaven produced the multitude and established rulers over them to govern and shepherd the people — how dare I shrink from toil and leave that one region alone without my grace!

sentences.zh: 必如公言，是古之帝王皆無征伐也！」

translations.literal: If it must be as you say, then the emperors of antiquity undertook no campaigns at all!"
translations.idiomatic: If it must be as you say, then the emperors of antiquity undertook no campaigns at all!"

sentences.zh: 道安曰：「必不得已，陛下宜駐蹕洛陽，遣使者奉尺書於前，諸將總六師於後，彼必稽首入臣，不必親涉江、淮也。」

translations.literal: Dao An said: "If it cannot be avoided, Your Majesty should halt your carriage at Luoyang, send envoys bearing a letter ahead, and have the generals command the six armies behind — they will surely bow and submit as your subjects. There is no need for you to cross the Yangtze and Huai in person."
translations.idiomatic: Dao An said, "If it cannot be avoided, Your Majesty should halt your carriage at Luoyang, send envoys bearing a letter ahead, and have the generals command the six armies behind — they will surely bow and submit as your subjects. There is no need for you to cross the Yangtze and Huai in person.

sentences.zh: 堅不聽。

translations.literal: Fu Jian did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian would not listen.

sentences.zh: 堅所幸張夫人諫曰：「妾聞天地之生萬物，聖王之治天下，皆因其自然而順之，故功無不成。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang, whom Fu Jian favored, remonstrated: "I have heard that when Heaven and Earth produce the myriad things, and when sage kings govern the realm, all follow their natural course — therefore nothing fails of success.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang, whom Fu Jian favored, remonstrated, "I have heard that when Heaven and Earth produce the myriad things, and when sage kings govern the realm, all follow their natural course — therefore nothing fails of success.

sentences.zh: 是以黃帝服牛乘馬，因其性也；

translations.literal: Therefore the Yellow Emperor rode oxen and drove horses — following their nature;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Yellow Emperor rode oxen and drove horses — following their nature;

sentences.zh: 禹浚九川，障九澤，因其勢也；

translations.literal: Yu dredged the nine rivers and dammed the nine marshes — following their terrain;
translations.idiomatic: Yu dredged the nine rivers and dammed the nine marshes — following their terrain;

sentences.zh: 后稷播殖百穀，因其時也；

translations.literal: Hou Ji sowed and planted the hundred grains — following the seasons;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Ji sowed and planted the hundred grains — following the seasons;

sentences.zh: 湯、武帥天下而攻桀、紂，因其心也。

translations.literal: Tang and Wu led the realm to attack Jie and Zhou — following the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and Wu led the realm to attack Jie and Zhou — following the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 皆有因則成，無因則敗。

translations.literal: Where there is a basis, success follows; where there is none, failure follows.
translations.idiomatic: Where there is a basis, success follows; where there is none, failure follows.

sentences.zh: 今朝野之人皆言晉不可伐，陛下獨決意行之，妾不知陛下何所因也。

translations.literal: Now everyone at court and in the countryside says Jin cannot be attacked, yet Your Majesty alone is resolved to proceed — I do not know on what basis Your Majesty acts.
translations.idiomatic: Now everyone at court and in the countryside says Jin cannot be attacked, yet Your Majesty alone is resolved to proceed — I do not know on what basis Your Majesty acts.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『天聰明自我民聰明。』

translations.literal: The Documents say: "Heaven's clarity comes from the clarity of the people."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, "Heaven's clarity comes from the clarity of the people."

sentences.zh: 天猶因民，而況人乎！

translations.literal: Heaven itself follows the people — how much more should men!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven itself follows the people — how much more should men!

sentences.zh: 妾又聞王者出師，必上觀天道，下順人心。

translations.literal: I have also heard that when a king sends forth his army, he must look to Heaven above and follow the people's hearts below.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that when a king sends forth his army, he must look to Heaven above and follow the people's hearts below.

sentences.zh: 今人心既不然矣，請驗之天道。

translations.literal: Now the people's hearts are not with you — please test this against Heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: Now the people's hearts are not with you — please test this against Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 諺云：『雞夜鳴者不利行師，犬群嗥者宮室將空，兵動馬驚，軍敗不歸。』

translations.literal: A proverb says: "When cocks crow at night, it bodes ill for an army on the march; when dogs howl in packs, the palace will be emptied; when troops stir and horses start, the army is defeated and does not return."
translations.idiomatic: A proverb says, "When cocks crow at night, it bodes ill for an army on the march; when dogs howl in packs, the palace will be emptied; when troops stir and horses start, the army is defeated and does not return."

sentences.zh: 自秋、冬以來，眾雞夜鳴，群犬哀嗥，廄馬多驚，武庫兵器自動有聲，此皆非出師之祥也。」

translations.literal: Since autumn and winter, cocks have crowed at night, dogs have howled mournfully in packs, stable horses have often been startled, and weapons in the arsenal have moved of themselves with sound — none of these are auspicious signs for setting forth an army."
translations.idiomatic: Since autumn and winter, cocks have crowed at night, dogs have howled mournfully in packs, stable horses have often been startled, and weapons in the arsenal have moved of themselves with sound — none of these are auspicious signs for setting forth an army."

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「軍旅之事，非婦人所當預也！」

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "Military affairs are no concern of women!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "Military affairs are no concern of women!"

sentences.zh: 堅幼子中山公詵最有寵，亦諫曰：「臣聞國之興亡，系賢人之用捨。

translations.literal: Fu Jian's youngest son, Duke Shen of Zhongshan, who was most favored, also remonstrated: "I have heard that the rise and fall of a state depends on whether worthy men are employed or dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's youngest son, Duke Shen of Zhongshan, who was most favored, also remonstrated, "I have heard that the rise and fall of a state depends on whether worthy men are employed or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 今陽平公，國之謀主，而陛下違之；

translations.literal: Now Duke Rong of Yangping is the state's chief strategist, yet Your Majesty goes against him;
translations.idiomatic: Now Duke Rong of Yangping is the state's chief strategist, yet Your Majesty goes against him;

sentences.zh: 晉有謝安、桓沖，而陛下伐之，臣竊惑之。」

translations.literal: Jin has Xie An and Huan Chong, yet Your Majesty would attack it — I am deeply puzzled."
translations.idiomatic: Jin has Xie An and Huan Chong, yet Your Majesty would attack it — I am deeply puzzled."

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「天下大事，孺子安知！」

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "Great affairs of state — what would a child know!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "Great affairs of state — what would a child know!"

sentences.zh: 秦劉蘭討蝗，經秋冬不能滅。

translations.literal: In Qin, Liu Lan's campaign against the locusts continued through autumn and winter without exterminating them.
translations.idiomatic: In Qin, Liu Lan's campaign against the locusts continued through autumn and winter without exterminating them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，有司奏請徵蘭下廷尉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the responsible officials memorialized requesting that Lan be summoned before the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, the responsible officials memorialized requesting that Lan be summoned before the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅曰：「災降自天，非人力所能除，此由朕之失政，蘭何罪乎？」

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin said: "Calamity descends from Heaven — it cannot be removed by human effort. This is due to my own misgovernment — what crime has Lan committed?"
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian said, "Calamity descends from Heaven — it cannot be removed by human effort. This is due to my own misgovernment — what crime has Lan committed?"

sentences.zh: 是歲，秦大熟，上田畝收七十石，下者三十石，蝗不出幽州境，不食麻豆，上田畝收百石，下者五十石。

translations.literal: This year Qin enjoyed a great harvest: top fields yielded seventy shi per mu, the lowest thirty shi. The locusts did not leave Youzhou's borders and did not eat hemp or beans; top fields yielded one hundred shi per mu, the lowest fifty shi.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qin enjoyed a great harvest: top fields yielded seventy shi per mu, the lowest thirty shi. The locusts did not leave Youzhou's borders and did not eat hemp or beans; top fields yielded one hundred shi per mu, the lowest fifty shi.
